fixes.area: Light and exposure: room legibility
fixes.problem: The frame is almost all black. Proof f300 has a mean luma of 3.1% (sRGB), and only 5% of pixels sit above 10%. The side walls measure about 1.6% and the head wall about 0.4%, where the treatment asks for charcoal #1a1b1e (about 10%) falling to blue-black. The carpet measures about 7% blue, so it never reads as cobalt. The room's volume and the walls' converging lines never form, and only the table carries the one-point perspective. At contact-sheet or phone size the drop lands on a void: a small cluster of coloured dots in black. It is also a big step down from S02's well-exposed medium at the cut. Accidental text check: clean. There are no FONT objects, the only image is the screen atlas, and the CRT fields are flat; what looks like a pattern on the CRT sides is vent grilles.
fixes.fix: In build(), set sc.view_settings.exposure to about +0.6 to +1.0 EV in place of 0.0. Add a shot-local wall graze: one long, soft area light high on each side wall, light-linked to the wall panels only, so the acoustic bays read as charcoal and converge on the vanishing point. Tested at f300 (crit1-cine/probe/var_compare.png): variant A (mist 0.25, +0.6 EV) gives a mean of 4.7%; variant B (mist 0.15, +1.0 EV) gives 6.0%, the carpet reads cobalt, the panel rhythm appears and the CRT fields hold without clipping. B is the better still. Even B leaves the walls at about 4.5%, so the graze is still needed. After lifting, render two consecutive final-tier frames (12 spp, animated seed, moving camera) to check the walls and carpet for denoiser crawl.

fixes.area: Compositing: depth mist on the subject
fixes.problem: room.compositor() runs with its default mist_amount 0.55 (start 6 m, depth 46 m, linear) and mixes toward near-black (0.006, 0.008, 0.016). Synergy is 39.4 m from the lens, so he is blended about 40% toward black (0.55 x 33.4/46). The far terminals lose 30-36%. The subject at the vanishing point ends up the most-darkened thing in frame. At final tier his plates read as dim tan, not ivory, and his shoulders and arms dissolve into the black head wall.
fixes.fix: Call room.compositor(threshold=0.9, mist_amount=0.15-0.25) for S03. Add the rig owner's proposed backlight (tools/synergy_in_room.py rim_light: area light at SYNERGY_POS + (0.35, 1.05, 2.55) aimed at his chest, cool 0.86/0.91/1.0, 55-80 W), set visible_camera False and light-link it to bpy.data.collections['Synergy'] the way walnut_bounce does. It lifts the crown and shoulder edges off the head wall (crit1-cine/probe/him_var.png).

fixes.area: Framing: printer beat and bottom edge
fixes.problem: The 1.5 m push carries the foreground out of the bottom edge. Probe projections: the printer's centre sits at 0.83 of frame height at f257, 0.92 at f300 and 0.99 at f352. The stack's base goes from 0.92 to 1.07. The printer's chair is gone by f300. The second bar's feed (f321-341) lands on a stack top in the bottom 8% of frame, about 2 px soft, so the 'feeds on each bar onto a stack that only grows' gag reads once, not twice. The trolley also slides out at the bottom-right corner (f273-297, centre at 0.99 at f300) before the droid drags it back in. At f257 the chair's star base touches the bottom edge. Bottom-edge crops of a beige box sitting on the axis are tangents a design director will reject.
fixes.fix: Keep the approved lens, height and start position, but shorten or ease the push so the printer tray, its seat and the stack top stay at least 10% inside the bottom edge through f341. The probe fit (v = 0.188 + 5.04/d) puts the printer's centre at about 0.91 at f352 with 0.8 m of travel, against 0.99 now. Alternatively, keep 1.5 m and finish the ease by about f330 at about 1.0 m. Re-check that the trolley stays clear of the right edge between f273 and f297, or start the push from a slightly wider position so it never kisses the edge.

fixes.area: lighting bug: paper_fill (s03_the_drop.py paper_fill)
fixes.problem: PAPER_K has no effect. `pl.data = ff.data.copy()` keeps the foot fill's action (foot_fillAction), because set_state(1,'lit') keyed foot_fill.data.energy. At render time the fcurve overrides `pl.data.energy = ff.data.energy * k`. Measured: foot_fill 13.0 W and paper_fill 13.0 W (ratio 1.000) at f257/300/352, where 4.55 W was intended. So the floor stack and the fed sheets get the full foot fill that env_room deliberately keeps off the paper, and the stack is the brightest object in the lower frame (proof f257 stack mean about 27 of 255; with the fix about 11). Evidence: crit1-tech/insp2/log.txt (ENERGY lines) and crit1-tech/stack_cmp.png (left: as built, right: fixed).
fixes.fix: In paper_fill(), straight after `pl.data = ff.data.copy()`, call `pl.data.animation_data_clear()`, then set `pl.data.energy = ff.data.energy * k`. S03 is lit throughout, so a constant is right. Verified with crit1-tech/tools/variant.py: paper_fill now evaluates to 4.55 W and the stack sits under the subject as the docstring says.

fixes.area: temporal noise / flicker (render settings)
fixes.problem: The wide budget renders the final at 12 spp with use_animated_seed=True. The push eases to almost nothing from about f330 (3.4 mm/frame at f340, 0.3 at f348), so the last 20+ frames are effectively a held image and the edges boil. Final 1600x900, f341 to f342 (the camera moves about 2.5 mm, so every difference is noise): far table and screens mean diff 2.4, p99 31 levels; Synergy p99 31; slab p99 23; screen-edge pixels flip by more than 120 levels at (732,300) and (888,364). Walls and carpet are stable (p99 1). In the diff image the change sits on screen bezels, cords, his silhouette and grain in the slab: crit1-tech/final_diff_far.png.
fixes.fix: Use a fixed seed for this slow push: `room.render_budget(kind='wide', samples=args.samples or None, locked=True)`, or set `sc.cycles.use_animated_seed = False` after it. Verified at proof with the same spp: far-end diff at 341 to 342 fell from mean 4.01 / p99 48 to 1.04 / p99 12; Synergy from 4.62 to 0.72; even at full cruise (257 to 258) 4.03 fell to 1.90. No visible screen-door effect at 20 mm/frame. For the GPU finals, also pass an explicit sample count (for example --samples 32): the 'wide' budget clamps the final tier to 12 spp, which suited CPU but is low for emissive edges at 1600 px.

fixes.area: sync point legibility: printer feeds f257 / f321
fixes.problem: In code the feeds are exact: sheet0 hide_render switches 256 to 257 and lands f277; sheet1 switches 320 to 321 and lands f341. No warnings from check_room_sync. On screen, though, nothing happens on either downbeat. The approved camera sees the printer from behind, so the tray run (f257-268) is hidden. The sheet first shows as a dark 2-4 px sliver clearing the printer's left side at about f269-274, and the landing reads as a 1-2 frame skew of the stack top (f276/f340), 20 frames (1.25 beats) after the downbeat. Meanwhile the sound cues s03-printer-f257 and s03-printer-f321 (audio/cues.json) put the feed transient on 257/321, so sound and picture are 12-20 frames apart. Evidence: crit1-tech/sheet_flight.png (f266-276), crit1-tech/crop_feed1.png and crop_feed2.png.
fixes.fix: Give S03 its own room timeline (copy demo_timeline's S03-relevant events, as S04's room_timeline already does) and feed at f245 and f309 instead of 257 and 321. The sheet then drops visibly past the printer's silhouette on the downbeats and settles on the stack at f265/f329. Mirror the same feed frames in s04_padlock_glide.room_timeline so the stack count agrees (0.4 mm a sheet, unseen in S04). Tell the sound owner the visible drop is on 257/321 and the stack hit is on 265/329. If the director prefers the room timeline untouched, record it as an accepted offset instead.

fixes.area: Macro post legibility, f129-150 (camera DOF and the envelope's value)
fixes.problem: The beat the whole film rests on, ivory robot fingers posting a sealed envelope, does not read. At f/4 and 0.208 m the aperture is 25 mm wide, so depth of field is about 1 mm. The envelope stands about 18 mm nearer the lens than the slot rim and blurs by about 50 px at 1600 px wide. In proof f129 and f136 it is a soft grey slab across the top 40% of the frame. The fold and flap cannot be read, and the seal is a fuzzy blue rectangle. The envelope also reads grey, not white: its face measures about 184/255 against about 218 on the lid. The fingers are a brown and cream smudge clipped by the top-right corner, with no black joint band and no tip cap readable.
fixes.fix: For f129-157, stop down to f/11-f/16 (the treatment says 'f/4 equivalent', which allows it). Set focus on the envelope's seal and fold plane, about 5-8 mm above the slot, instead of the slot rim. Rack to the rim over f144-148 as the envelope disappears, then open toward FSTOP1 during the move. Raise ENV_RAKE from 0.8 W to about 2.5 W, or widen the card, so the envelope face reads white against the lid. Change PINCH_X and the approach so the index tip, with one black band and its bronze cap, sits about 10-15% inside the right edge instead of being cut off by it. Check f129, f136 and f142 at proof.

fixes.area: Performance and contact: the envelope shrink, f136-148
fixes.problem: stage_post scales the envelope toward the slot centre, but the fingers only follow PRESS_D = 2 mm and the pinch stays closed where it was. By f142 (scale 0.65) the end of the envelope is about 50 px clear of the pads at 800 px, so the fingers visibly pinch air while the paper slides out of them. The treatment's 'fingers press it edge-first into the slot' becomes a magic trick with a contact break that an ILM supervisor would reject.
fixes.fix: Pick one of two fixes. (a) Mechanical let-go: key the thumb and index pads apart by 2-3 mm over SINK0 to SINK0+2, so the slot visibly takes the envelope from an opening pinch. (b) Keep contact: drive the pinch point with the shrink, pinch_at[f] = c + (pinch - c) * s(f), until about 0.3 scale, then release. Either way, hold the hand still for 2 frames after release before LIFT0.

fixes.area: Steam, f129-177
fixes.problem: The treatment calls for two thin threads of steam rising past the lens. What renders is a milky, out-of-focus fog over the top third of the frame. In an A/B at f142 with STEAM_ALPHA=0, the top band is +60/255 brighter with steam: the cobalt carpet washes to grey and the fingers are veiled, so the steam actively hurts the frame. Puffs rise 0.17 m toward a lens 0.208 m above, into extreme defocus, so they can never read as threads.
fixes.fix: Keep the threads in the focal zone and have them cross the frame. Cut STEAM_RISE to about 0.03-0.04 m and drift the puffs sideways along the slot's long axis or across the lid (a draft), not toward the lens. Shrink the puff size so each thread is a thin wisp. Cut STEAM_GLOW and STEAM_ALPHA by about half and let them read against the dark band beyond the lid rim. With the f/11 change they will hold shape. If they still read as fog at proof, drop the steam rather than ship a haze.

fixes.area: Amber slot glow, f146-154
fixes.problem: At f148 the slot is a flat pale peach pill (core about sRGB 242,198,164) inside a hotter near-white rim (about 253,233,213), with no warm light on the lid around it. It reads as a sticker or an LED button, not 'a warm amber glow pulsing up out of the slot'. AgX desaturates the hot emission, and the s02_slot_glow point light (0.03 W peak) adds almost no spill.
fixes.fix: Lower GLOW_PEAK but feed a more saturated amber (about #FF8A2A), so AgX keeps the hue below its highlight rolloff. Make the glow brightest at the centre of the well and darker at the lip, not the reverse. Raise the s02_slot_glow light 5-10x (about 0.2-0.3 W peak) so the raised spout lip, the inner rim and the lid next to the slot catch warm light that rises and falls with the pulse.

fixes.area: Camera move pacing and reveal order, f157-232
fixes.problem: With MOVE_SHAPE (2.0, 3.6) the camera's speed peaks at about 2.0 m/s around f185-189. The lanyard V, badge, chest plates and chip, neck pistons, boom mic and face all go by in about 20 frames (f177-197). The face enters the frame at f191-193, near peak speed, and SHUTTER closes to 0.2 only to hide the smear. Then f197-229 is a 0.7 m creep-out that shows nothing new. The treatment's sequential 'rises past ... and finally the face' never registers, and the badge is never featured.
fixes.fix: Rebalance the profile to be flatter and later, for example MOVE_SHAPE of about (1.6, 1.9), or split the path into two stages. The vertical reveal (cup, then lanyard and badge, chest and chip, pistons, mic, face) should then take about 45 frames, and the face should land with at least 15 frames of settle before f232. Then remove the SHUTTER dip and keep 180 degrees for the whole shot, so the motion texture does not change partway through the move.

fixes.area: Camera height: looking down into the collar cavity, about f177-196
fixes.problem: The camera path stays at 1.50-1.57 m while it passes the shoulders, so the lens looks down into the open top of the torso. In animatic f185 (and still in proof f196) the black cavity with the A-frame rising out of it reads as an open cardboard box. That frame cannot be printed.
fixes.fix: Lower the middle control points of Move.B to about 1.35-1.40 m, so the lens passes the chest at or below shoulder height and cranes up to END_H 1.58 m as it settles. That is also the 'rises past' feel the treatment describes. If the cavity still shows at level framing, send the rig owner a request for a collar plate. Do not fix it in the shot.

fixes.area: End-frame composition and colour bokeh, f232-256
fixes.problem: END_DIST = 2.90 is needed to hold both the face and the badge, but the centred figure then fills only the middle ~55% of the frame width, with dead black on both sides. The cup sits at x = 0.40 (the centre column), not the treatment's lower-left third. The bokeh does not deliver the treatment's 'cobalt, acid yellow, pink, sky'. Cobalt, the brand colour and first in the list, is the dimmest disc (about 0,30,79) and touches the right edge of the frame. Orange (Operations, not in the list) is the most prominent disc. All six discs sit in one band along the top edge, which looks scattered rather than composed. The bottom edge also cuts through the dark waist gap with its orange and red cables.
fixes.fix: Keep the distance, but move the composition off centre: shift or aim so the head sits a little right of centre and the cup lands on the left third line (or raise END_ANG to about 16-18 degrees and re-check the wedge and earcup read). Call room.front_bokeh with a chosen region, seed and n so that cobalt, acid yellow, pink and sky are the four discs that read, at 60-90 px on a 1600 px frame, none within about 5% of an edge. Place one beside the head on the right and one lower-left in the void, not all along the top. Check the bottom-edge crop against the badge at the same time.

fixes.area: performance / camera timing (f410-418)
fixes.problem: The shot's only performance beat happens off screen. The finger's descent is fully keyed: index tip z goes from 0.993 to 0.753 over f410-418, eased, and holds still with no flinch. But the camera is still swinging, so the tip projects to image x=2.49 at f410, 1.19 at f416 and 0.90 at f418. report() also prints 'hand first in frame f418'. The treatment says 'At f410 Synergy's left index fingertip lowers into frame top-right' in 'one clean 8-frame move'. On screen, the hand is never seen arriving. A finger that has already landed slides in from the right edge during a whip pan (f418-422: hand x 0.90 to 0.55 while the padlock moves 0.18 to 0.41), so hand and padlock seem to converge, like a grab instead of a waiting fingertip. Evidence: crit1-cine/contact_land.png, logs/probe.log.
fixes.fix: Finish the camera's heading swing, and get the stop zone into frame top-right, by f406-408 at the latest. Then the whole 8-frame descent plays in a nearly settled frame. In practice: start the pass-by or swing earlier (ORBIT/AIM ending around f404, not f418/f422), or ride behind and beside the padlock looking up the travel line, so that at f410 the padlock sits in the lower-left third and the stop zone 2.2 m ahead is upper-right. Add a gate to report(): hand first in frame must be ≤ f410, and the tip image position at f410 must fall inside x 0.55-0.95, y 0.55-0.95.

fixes.area: composition of the hold (f424-432) / contact read
fixes.problem: The bronze fingertip is hidden behind the padlock for the whole hold. A ray from the lens to the index tip hits padlock_kevin_body on every frame f424-432. The camera ends about 126 deg round from the travel line, behind and to +X, and the slide line runs straight into the tip. The 'stops dead against one fingertip' gag therefore never reads, and the canon bronze tip cap is never shown. The f418-428 rack from padlock to fingertip is invisible because the target is 22 mm behind the padlock and occluded. Continuity: S09 already offsets its slide line 22 mm to his right (SLIDE_OFFSET=0.022) so the brass meets the tip with its camera-right shoulder and the tip stays visible. S04's centred contact therefore does not match the 'identical' repeat.
fixes.fix: Use S09's contact. Run the slide line 22 mm to his right of the tip (stop_for with the offset start/tip, as in s09_same_padlock.py), so that from the +X-side lens the bronze tip shows beside the brass's right shoulder. Alternatively, end the camera at ≤95 deg from the travel line. Re-check with a lens-to-tip ray, which should come back clear for f424-432, then let the rack land on a visible tip.

fixes.area: camera move (f384-422)
fixes.problem: The treatment's lateral track ('tracks toward the head at the padlock's speed, holding it in the lower third'; decelerates f416-424) became a 110 deg orbit-pan. Heading goes from 160 to 50 deg, peaking at 5.3 deg/frame (127 deg/s) over f396-404, which is about 88 px of motion-blur smear on the background at final res. In this window the padlock rides at the frame middle (image y 0.44-0.51 from the bottom), not the lower third. From about f397 to f415 it is seen edge-on as a thin sliver, so its shackle-and-body silhouette is lost for about 0.75 s, and the upper 60% of the frame is empty black (f401-f414). These frames do not survive as stills and do not fit the film's rigid, deadpan camera grammar. The dolly also starts braking at f404, not f416.
fixes.fix: Keep pan rates ≤2.5 deg/frame, eased. Keep the padlock's broad face at ≤45 deg to the lens throughout the ride. Tilt up or add lens shift so the padlock rides on the lower third and the terminal colour discs (Keys cobalt, Synthia ivory) fill the upper frame behind it. If a pass-by pan is kept, place it early (about f386-402), at ≥0.5 m lateral distance, so it ends with the lens looking up the line. Move the dolly brake toward f412-424 so the overtake into centre happens on the treatment's frames.

fixes.area: frame content: rest of him in shot
fixes.problem: From f415 to the end of the hold, fragments of his body sit in the top-right quarter: red and orange waist cables at the top centre, a cream hip plate behind the hand, and a cream thigh or pelvis trapezoid on the walnut horizon to the right of the hand. That last one reads as an unexplained object sitting on the table. The treatment says 'Only his left index finger and the back of his hand ... The rest of him is off frame.' At f/2.8 and about 1 m these are not soft enough to vanish (see proof/s04/0432.png, zoom_432.png).
fixes.fix: In this shot, set visible_camera=False on the pelvis, thigh and hip plates and the waist cables (keep their shadows and glossy contribution), or re-aim or tilt so they fall outside the frame. Result: only the forearm, back-of-hand plate and index break the dark top-right.

fixes.area: light / walnut look
fixes.problem: The walnut never delivers the treatment's 'mirror full of long coloured streaks' crossed by the skylight slab as 'a hard bright band'. In f353-388 it reads as a dusty mauve (sampled sRGB ≈ 98,77,73 lower-left), against S03's dark neutral walnut (≈ 43,37,33): a visible cut mismatch at f353. From f398 to the end it is flat brown-black (0-12), with no slab band and no terminal streaks, so the lower half of the hold is a muddy reflection. The only time the slab shows is as a saturated yellow defocused stripe at f393-395, which reads as tape, not 6500K daylight.
fixes.fix: Find what tints the grazing walnut pink: likely the reflected wall or carpet, or the compositor's mist or haze colour at this lens. Neutralise it toward S03's walnut. For the 3 cm lens, add glossy-only terminal-colour streak cards (light-linked to the walnut, as the room's streak cards are) and a bright glossy band, for example the slab's spill on the head wall, so that the walnut mirrors coloured streaks and a cool hard band near the horizon in the ride and the hold.

fixes.area: sync: fingertip beat f410 (TREATMENT S04)
fixes.problem: The treatment says that at f410 the left index 'lowers into frame top-right' in one clean 8-frame move, and that move never appears on screen. I checked visibility frame by frame with ray tests from the camera to the rig's vertices: no part of the left hand is in frame until f418. It enters from the right edge at image (0.896, 0.540), already resting, mid-height rather than top-right, and only because the pan carries it in. At f410 the fingertip projects to image x=2.50 (off screen); at f416 it is at x=1.19. The lowering at f410-418 is keyed correctly: a straight vertical, eased, tip z 0.9985 to 0.7585 at x,y (0.2907, -0.0924). It is just never filmed. The script's own report() says 'hand first in frame f418'.
fixes.fix: Re-block the camera so the hover above the stop is already in frame top-right by f410 and the whole f410-418 lowering is seen. One option: end the swing behind-beside the padlock (BETA_END around 140-150 deg, ORBIT ending around 408) so the lens looks up-table toward the fingertip during f410-418, then ease to the final frame. Keep the finger keys and the s04-fingertip-rest cue at f418 as they are. Add an assert in report() that the index_3_L tip projects inside the frame (x<1, y>0.6) on f410.

fixes.area: camera: pan reverses direction f386
fixes.problem: The signed heading per frame (measured from cam.matrix_world) pans right +0.035 to +1.05 deg/frame over f378-385, passes zero at f386-387 (+0.19, then -0.43), then pans left, accelerating to -5.31 deg/frame at f401-402. That is a reversal inside one move. It shows on the far bokeh in the animatic: Operations' orange disc drifts right about 11% of frame width over f377-386, then swings back left (contact_panrev.png). It reads as a hitch two frames before the f388 flash. The cause is ride_aim (line 299): its 12-frame blend from the approved s04_start offset to FRAME_RIDE x=+0.12 pans right while the ORBIT that starts at f384 pans left.
fixes.fix: Make the heading monotonic. Either drop the rightward reframe (FRAME_RIDE[0] equal to the start's own offset), or start the orbit at f377 and drive the reframe blend with the same trap() curve so its rightward component never outruns the orbit. Add a check in key() that the sign of dh never flips between f377 and f422.

fixes.area: flicker: locked hold f424-432
fixes.problem: The camera, padlock, hand and focus are all static from f428 (camera static from f424). I diffed consecutive proof renders of the hold. f429 vs f430: mean abs diff 1.52/255, 3.6% of pixels differ by more than 10/255, peak 181. f430 vs f431: 1.53/255, 3.8%. The diff image is classic OIDN blotch boil across the walnut reflections, the brass face, the master cord and the hand edges (diff_429_430_x12.png). The cause is render_budget(kind='macro') at line 489: it runs with locked=False, so use_animated_seed=True on frames whose camera is locked. The final tier (16 spp, adaptive 0.03) lowers the boil but does not remove it.
fixes.fix: Fix the sampling seed on the static frames only. For example, register a frame_change_pre handler in build(): sc.cycles.use_animated_seed = sc.frame_current < 424. Keep the animated seed while the camera moves. Re-check with three consecutive proofs (429-431); the target is under 0.5% of pixels differing by more than 10/255.

fixes.area: sync: rack focus f418-428 does not read
fixes.problem: The rack is keyed on the treatment's frames, but it only moves focus 17 mm. The focus distance goes 0.4574 m (f418, on the padlock) to 0.5711 (f424) to 0.5766 (f428), while the padlock sits at 0.5593 m from f424. At 40 mm f/2.8 focused near 0.57 m the depth of field is about 0.553-0.588 m, so the padlock and finger are both sharp before and after. The treatment's 'rack focus from padlock to fingertip' is not visible on screen. Between f418 and f424 the focus mostly tracks the padlock's own approach.
fixes.fix: This resolves with the blocker's re-block: from behind-beside the padlock, the fingertip is 0.3-0.5 m beyond it at f418, so the rack covers a real distance. Otherwise, rack across a separation of at least 0.15 m or open the stop for the end beat. Verify by rendering f418 and f428 at proof and checking that sharpness swaps between padlock and fingertip.

fixes.area: Post f500-519 (contact, shrink, glow): the shot's payoff
fixes.problem: The padlock never reaches the lid. At contact (f508) its lowest point is 33.7 mm above the slot (DIAG), which reads as about 5 cm in frame (crit1-cine/proof/s05/0508.png). The shrink (line ~1091: scale 0.02^(t^2) toward a point 6 mm under the slot) keeps the padlock's lowest point above the slot plane until about f515. So from f510 to f514 a shrinking gold speck floats in mid-air in front of the chest plate and disappears there on f519 (crit1-cine/post.png, crit1-cine/proof_post_crops.png). The lens sees the lid at about 7 deg, so the slot is invisible and the lid never hides anything. 'Posted without looking' reads as a vanishing trick, and the sound's lid touch (f508) and plip (f512, audio/CUES.md) land on an object hanging in the air. At contact the lens also sees the padlock's keyway underside, so it reads as a gold box with a round dial, not a padlock. S07 repeats this posting action eight times.
fixes.fix: Release on f508 and let the padlock drop: key its translation down the slot axis so its lowest point meets the slot plane on f510 (34 mm under gravity is 2 frames, eased in), with no scale change before that. Then shrink f510-518 toward a point 12-15 mm under the slot plane, so the lid's near rim covers it from the bottom up: at least half of it below the lid line on f512, nothing above the lid after f514. This matches the treatment's 'contact f508, shrink f510-518' exactly and puts the plip on a padlock that is half inside the lid. At contact, turn the padlock in the grip so the lens sees its profile with the shackle up (or its broad face), not the keyway underside. Check with proof crops at f508, 510, 512 and 514.

fixes.area: Arm silhouette while posting, f504-524
fixes.problem: rig.post_pose's contact pose (extent 44 mm) puts the left forearm in a horizontal bar across the base of the neck at shoulder height, with the elbow winged out to frame right. After the release, the empty hand hovers as a claw beside the neck from f510 to f520 (crit1-cine/proof/s05/0517.png, crit1-cine/carry.png). This hides the neck A-frame, cuts the figure in two under the chin and reads as an arm across his throat. The exit (f520-524) then wipes sideways across the chest at shoulder height before it drops. For 20 frames there is no printable still.
fixes.fix: Once the drop closes the gap, the hand can release higher, so solve the contact with your own place_arm_clear search instead of rig.post_pose's single solution. Try hand frames with the fingers pointing down and forward and the elbow below the shoulder: penalise pole z > -0.3 and a wrist above the collar line. Add a score term for how much the forearm overlaps the neck band in image space (head's lowest facet to collar), the same way hand_over_face already scores cover of the screen. After the release, withdraw at once along the same line (no 7-frame hover by the neck), then exit straight down at frame right.

fixes.area: Look of the hero padlock in the study, f441-500

fixes.area: Exit f521-528: the hand lowers out of frame

fixes.area: Light: the colleague colour chase
fixes.problem: Measured on his chest plate during each flare (hue, saturation, lightness): burgundy f609 is 11 degrees, 0.27, 0.57; pink f657 is 17 degrees, 0.21, 0.57, so the two match. fixes.area: interpenetration: palm inside binder f728-737
fixes.problem: Over the cup the hand is buried in the binder. Ray-parity depth of the left palm and fingers inside the binder: 37.7 mm at f728, 38.4 at f729, 38.8 at f730, 38.6 at f731, 37.6 at f732, 34.6 at f733, 31.4 at f734, 27.9 at f735, 16.8 at f736, 6.1 at f737. fixes.area: elbow pops (every cycle and the binder)
fixes.problem: 20 single-frame flips of the arm plane by 59-144 deg, with the elbow bent 90-120 deg: f616 84, f622 79, f632 77, f638 65, f648 88, f654 78, f664 77, f670 65, f676 77, f679 86, f684 65, f687 86, f692 65, f695 86, f700 77, f716 133, f725 66, f726 81, f727 59, f748 144. fixes.area: held problems flip in the pinch
fixes.problem: Some problems spin in the fingers in a single frame. Rotation per frame: Keys' and People's envelopes turn 130 deg on f630->631 and f662->663. Strategy's first tabs turn 161 deg and jump 11 cm on f644->645, the frame after the grip. Arjun's tabs and Strategy's second tabs turn 143 deg on f674->675 and f698->699. If a turn cannot clear the fingers in time, open the pinch a few mm rather than jump. Keep scale monotonic from SHRINK_FROM to contact.

fixes.problem: The picture rhythm is not S04's rhythm and does not match the S09 sound. room_timeline calls terminals['kevin'].speak(833, 869, seed=7), which produces four syllables at f833 (8), f841 (9), f852 (6) and f858 (6), ending f866. fixes.area: staging / the knock (f852)
fixes.problem: The padlock stops directly between the lens and the fingertip, so the contact is invisible. Its centre stops at (0.2887, -0.1089), 19 mm down-table of the tip at (0.29, -0.09) and nearly on the lens axis. From the camera the tip projects only about 5 mm right of the padlock centre, inside its roughly 22 mm half-width. In crit1-cine/zknock.png the bronze index tip is clear on the walnut at f833 and fully hidden by f852. What reads is a padlock stopping in front of a hand whose three curled fingers hang about 5 cm above the walnut. 'Stops against his fingertip with the same knock' is lost, and the visual rhyme with S04 (where the finger is visible) is lost too.
fixes.fix: In padlock_slide, offset the slide line about 20-24 mm toward his right (-X, frame left), parallel to dirn. Keep stop_for(..., hand=rig.parts_on_bones(HAND_L)) so the contact stays real (a 1.5 mm gap). The brass then meets the tip with its camera-right shoulder. Verify with world_to_camera_view that at least 8 mm of the bronze tip shows beside the padlock at f852, and that the padlock still makes contact; beyond about 30 mm it misses the finger.

fixes.area: performance / the look-down (f857-868)
fixes.problem: 'For the first time he looks down at a problem' does not read as looking at the padlock. Measured: with a 12 deg pitch and no turn, the face normal ends 9.2 deg below horizontal and meets the walnut 4.6 m down-table. That is 58.9 deg off the padlock but only 28.8 deg off the lens. From this low frontal lens the move squares the face plate to camera, and the face centre moves only 13 px at 1600x900. It reads as Synergy looking into the lens, not at the padlock at frame right by his left hand. The 1-LED eye drop (dy=1) is the only cue.
fixes.fix: Keep the treatment's 12 deg pitch and the eased timing (f857-868 down, f921-928 up). Point the eyes at the padlock with tl.look(857, 920, dx=1, dy=1) (+1 column is his left, toward frame right); the return stays hidden in the blink. Ideally also add a small turn toward his left (head z +6 to +8 deg) in the same single eased move and in the lift, so the face visibly turns toward the padlock. It is still one mechanical move and still not a dip. Re-measure the angle to the padlock against the angle to the lens.

fixes.area: light / still quality
fixes.problem: The lighting is flat front fill with no hierarchy, so the eye goes to the badge and chest, not to the face where the whole performance happens. Proof f891 luminance: head enamel 136, chest grey panel 176, chest cream 158, pelvis plate 159, cup 182, badge 232 (the brightest object in frame, dead centre). The warm walnut bounce now lights the pelvis as brightly as the head. An ILM supervisor would call it a product turntable, not a tension beat.
fixes.fix: Shape the light toward the head. Narrow Kevin's key (smaller spread, aimed at the screen and upper chest) so it falls off down the torso. Drop BOUNCE_E so the pelvis plate sits about one stop under the head enamel; it should still show, per the rig note, but subordinate. Keep the skylight top key and the rims. Target: head enamel at least as bright as the chest panels, and the badge no longer the frame's hottest large patch.

fixes.area: sync: Kevin's key vs sound and S04
fixes.problem: room_timeline calls terminals['kevin'].speak(833, 869, seed=7), and the docstring says this is 'identical rhythm to S04: seed 7'. It is not. S04 keys Kevin's screen with kevin_speaks() on the murmur bursts SYLLABLES=((353,8),(361,8),(369,8)). speak(seed=7) gives syllables at 833(8f), 841(9f), 852(6f) and 858(6f), then holds steady from f866. The cue sheet plays the S04 bursts again at f833, f841 and f849 (8 frames each). Measured on the animatic, the face key is in a trough at f849-852 and pulses up again on f853, one frame after the knock, so it reads as a flash reacting to the knock. A fourth light 'syllable' at f859-862 has no murmur and plays while his head goes down. Kevin's sky bokeh disc pulses the same wrong rhythm.
fixes.fix: Replace the speak() call with S04's kevin_speaks grammar (import it or copy it) keyed on SYLLABLES=((833,8),(841,8),(849,8)), which is S04's +480, with the same SPEAK_PULSE and SPEAK_BAND. The key then holds steady from f857, the frame the look-down and its servo tick start. Update SPEAK and the docstring to match. Do not change the audio: the identical sample is the joke.

fixes.area: flicker: Kevin key on the hero
fixes.problem: The s09_kevin_key driver passes the raw screen channels straight into the area light that keys his face and chest: gain, plus bamt, whose syllable-end keys are CONSTANT. The result is a sawtooth: it ramps up over 4 frames and drops in 1. In the every-frame animatic, face luminance steps 10-13% in a single frame at 839>840, 852>853, 856>857 and 862>863 (chest about 8%). Each step changes about 30-35k px (14% of the frame) by more than 8 levels. On a visible CRT this reads as speech; as an off-screen key on the hero it reads as electrical flicker. Peak to trough is +78% in energy (30.6 to 54.6 W).
fixes.fix: Drive the key from a smoothed envelope instead of the screen channels. Key lt.data.energy per frame with a raised-cosine bump per syllable (rest 1.0, peak about 1.3, LINEAR keys, no CONSTANT steps), or drop the bamt term and smooth gain. Aim for no frame-to-frame change above about 4%, and keep the rest level after the speech equal to the envelope's base so f857 does not step down.

fixes.area: performance / contact (f945-992)
fixes.problem: The jack is never actually held. I measured the gap with a BVH nearest-surface probe (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-linkedin/35346f8e-3086-50e0-b336-b295d0b54106/scratchpad/shots/s10/crit1-cine/probe/contact.py). From the grip at f945 to the last frame at f992, the closest hand surfaces stay 2.9-3.1 mm (index_3_L) and 4.1-4.9 mm (thumb_2_L) away from jack_barrel/pin/relief. During the rock, index_2_L opens to 8-9 mm. The final-quality crops show it clearly (finalcrop/s10/0945.png, 0975.png): dark carpet is visible between the index and the knurl, and the thumb cap hovers above the barrel. Through the held beat, the pull and the dangle, the jack levitates between the fingers and rocks +/-14 deg about a point in the air. The script's contact report only tests for overlap, so it prints 'none' and misses this. The rig's thumb_pinch(gap=0.0099) does not produce the pad-to-knurl air it promises. The fault is either in the shot's pinch geometry or in synergy.py's pad radii (PAD_R_INDEX/PAD_R_THUMB against the mesh); report it to the rig owner.
fixes.fix: Close the pinch to real contact. Measure each pad's nearest distance to the jack per frame (BVHTree.find_nearest over the index_3_L and thumb_2_L meshes) and shrink GAP, or shift the pinch point, until both pads sit 0-0.3 mm into the knurl (slight compression reads as grip). Add a gate to report() that fails if any pad is more than 0.5 mm off the jack on f945-992. Re-stage the post-pull motion so the read is physical. One option: a rigid pinch with no rock, where the coil carries the two damped cycles. The other: from f964 the jack pivots about the pad contact axis (the pinch axis through the pads, not the 'side' axis in the air) and hangs pin-down, swaying two damped cycles, which is the treatment's 'dangles from his fingers and sways'. S11 imports key_jack and left_hand, so re-check S11's f993-995 hand-over and the jack_drop start.

fixes.area: framing / story (hub and cord)
fixes.problem: The treatment's key composition element is missing: 'its yellow coiled cord rises to the black starfish conference hub behind it (soft): the root that every terminal's cord runs into'. The probe puts the hub at image (-0.11, 1.24), well off frame. Only 8 of 37 cord sample points on the walnut top fall in frame. Swinging the approved s10_jack_macro (a low look-back along the cord with the soft hub behind) round to az 64 / el 16 kept the arm out of the lens but cut the jack off from the meeting. The audience sees a jack in the side of a table, not the master plug, which weakens the S10 to S11 cause and effect. The 16 deg view also makes the vertical apron face of the table ~45% of every frame: a featureless brown field with smeared finger reflections. The glossy walnut top, where the CRT pools and the slab should streak, is a sliver.
fixes.fix: Return toward the approved geometry: look back along the master cord from about az 28-38 deg (the hub-to-socket line is about az 36), el 5-12 deg, 0.45-0.55 m, with shift_y keeping the socket and knurl in the lower third and the soft hub plus converging cords in the upper third. To clear his arm, push the camera further out along that line rather than swinging sideways. Make the hand's approach come from above the frame top: extend solve_grip's 'looks' to include the hub and the cord run, so the sight term keeps the forearm out of them. Gate it in report(): the hub's world_to_camera_view must be inside 0.1-0.9 on every frame. Note that at 100 mm the treatment's 'high three-quarter' and the hub cannot both be in frame; the director's low look-back with the hub wins.

fixes.area: light / palette (colleague bokeh)
fixes.problem: The colleagues' colour glow is gone for most of the shot. The four re-laid discs sit at image x 0.76-0.98, exactly where his forearm and hand go. From f937 they are mostly covered, and from f963 to f992 there is no terminal colour in frame at all, leaving only brown, navy, ivory and gold. The treatment wants 'a distant terminal colour glow in the bokeh behind', and the colours need to be alive here so their death in S11 lands. The discs are also on the wrong side: the terminals are down-table, which this lens sees at frame left and top, not over the carpet behind him at frame right. The operations disc is clipped by the top-right corner at f929.
fixes.fix: With the reframe, re-lay BOKEH points in the band beyond the walnut horizon, down-table and behind the hub, where the screens really are. Ray-test each disc against his hand and arm on every frame (not only f929) so at least three colours stay visible through f992. Keep discs fully inside the frame or fully out, with no corner tangents. If the walnut top is in frame, let the CRT colours streak on it.

fixes.area: performance legibility (finger close f936-945, held beat f945-960)
fixes.problem: The coil arches through the hand. From f937 to f960 the master cord runs in front of the thumb and middle finger, so the canon one-at-a-time close (index f937, middle f939, thumb f941) does not read: the middle finger is never seen, and the thumb lands behind the coil. The 16-frame held beat, the longest still in the shot, reads as a hand tangled in a spring rather than a precise mechanical pinch on the knurl.
fixes.fix: Choose a pinch orientation in which the cord's tail leaves away from the lens. Alternatively, use CORD_MIDS (provided for this insert) to route the overhang so it rises behind the hand rather than in front of it. Each finger's close should silhouette cleanly against the walnut or the carpet. Check with an animatic run every 2 frames over f933-947.

fixes.area: cord action (f964-982)
fixes.problem: 'The yellow coil springs, then relaxes across the walnut' is not on screen. In frame, the coil snaps from its arch to a taut straight diagonal from the frame top to the jack tail by about f968, then freezes through f992. It reads as stretched under tension, not relaxed. The settle across the walnut happens off frame.
fixes.fix: Give MasterCord.pulled's in-frame span a visible overshoot and two damped settles into a soft sag, not a straight line. Once the reframe brings the walnut top in, keep the relax on screen. The cord should end slack, matching the dead meeting.

fixes.area: grip contact (f945-992)
fixes.problem: The pads never touch the knurl. Exact BVH distance, measured both ways (probe2.log), from the f945 grip through the pull and to f992: the thumb is 4.69 mm from jack_barrel and the index tip 3.03 mm (2.9-4.3 mm after the pull). That's a 17.5 mm opening around a 9.8 mm knurl, about 7.7 mm more air than GAP=0.0099 asks for. So he pulls out and carries a jack he isn't holding, and the gap shows at proof res (crit1-tech/zoom_pinch.png, f945/966/992). The f945 'pads bite' beat moves the thumb 0.08 mm, so the grip click cued at f945 (cues.json s10-grip) has no visible contact. The shot's S10_DEBUG report says 'none' because it only tests interpenetration, never the gap.
fixes.fix: In s10_jack.py (GAP l.93, thumb_rots l.271), measure pad-to-barrel distance after solve_grip, by mesh distance from the thumb_2_L/index_3_L parts to jack_barrel at F_GRIP. Shrink GAP (about 2.2 mm here) or iterate until both pads sit 0.0-0.3 mm off the knurl with no overlap. Also check the err and pad_gap that rig.thumb_pinch returns. Key the f944-945 bite as a visible 0.3-0.5 mm squeeze. Add an assert to report(): pad distance <=0.3 mm on f945-992. Rig owner: thumb_pinch's PAD_R_INDEX/PAD_R_THUMB pad model leaves about 7.7 mm extra air at gap 9.9 mm with index angles (18,44,30). Check pad_gap on the S02/S05/S07 posts too.

fixes.area: master cord vs jack (f967-992, into S11)
fixes.problem: From f967 on, the coil's last turns pass through the black strain relief, then end in a pig-tail loop beyond it. In probe2.log, jack_relief overlaps the coil by 122/242/224/140 triangle pairs at f967-970, 102 at f979, and 44-56 at f982-994, up to 12 mm from the attach point. Up to 64 of the overlap centroids per frame are visible to the lens, at frame centre, through the final hold (crit1-tech/tail_zoom.png). Cause: `tail`/`tail2` ride on the jack, but mid3/mid4 are keyed only by MasterCord.pulled(), which relaxes them -6 mm Y / -4 mm Z. Meanwhile the jack has moved +24 mm Y / +17 mm Z and then swings ±14°, so the order-3 curve has to fold back over the 12 mm tail2 lead.
fixes.fix: After room.master.pulled(F_PULL), add the jack's own per-frame displacement to the near-jack mids: the pull offset from PULL plus the swing rotation about the pinch, weighted mid4 1.0, mid3 about 0.6, mid2 about 0.25. Alternatively, put a Child Of on mid4 to the jack root with influence keyed 0 to 1 over f960-963. Then check coil vs jack_relief overlap each frame (ignore 3 mm at the tail) in report(). Put this in one function (for example S10.cord_follow(room, M0, sol)) that S11's s10_handover also calls. S11 rebuilds the cord with its own pulled() call, so a fix that lives only in S10.build() would pop the cord at the f992 to f993 cut.

fixes.area: fingers into walnut (f930-940)
fixes.problem: During the approach, Synergy_middle_3_L, ring_2/3_L and pinky_2/3_L go into the walnut: 30/129/118/99/101/100/110/130/133/87/14 triangle pairs on f930-940 (probe2.log). Every pair is inside the frame, with 3-11 overlap centroids per frame visible to the lens. You can see defocused fingers sinking into the head-edge face left of the jack (crit1-tech/walnut_zoom.png, f933/f937). ready_offset() only clears the jack, socket and cord (hand_overlaps l.456-468), so the -40 mm X ready point it picked was never tested against the table. The final grip pose itself is clear (0 pairs from f941).
fixes.fix: Add R.walnut_objects(room) to the overlap set that ready_offset tests over F_DESC0-F_INDEX+1. Also hold middle/ring/pinky at their GRIP curl (or between OPEN and GRIP) during the descent so the tips stay tucked, or add a +Y component to the ready offset (away from the edge face). Add arm-vs-walnut to report() for f929-992.

fixes.area: continuity (headset hand-over S11 -> S13 -> S14)
fixes.problem: headset_on_walnut (s13_first_sip.py lines 274-320) ignores S11's HEADSET_REST. S11 sets the headset down at ((0.30, -0.25, 0.8221), quat (0.70182, -0.0867, -0.08595, 0.70182)) and holds it to its cut; it is visible in S11 f1150-1152. S13 re-poses it at (0.34, -0.12, z) with Ry(-90), which is 13.6 cm away and about 112 deg rotated. S14 copies S13's rest ('where S13 left it'), so the headset visibly jumps between S11's last frame and S14's top-down f1345, where it sits large beside the hub. It is off screen in S13, but S13 owns the hand-over.
fixes.fix: Start from S11.HEADSET_REST, either moved into a shared constant or copied verbatim: set hs.location and hs.rotation_quaternion to it at START-10 instead of the (0.34, -0.12) / Ry(-90) solve. Then key the f1318-1334 slide of +0.035 m X from that rest. Keep the cord-hook (0, 0, 1) workaround. Update s14_circle_back.headset_on_walnut to the same rest plus 0.035 m. Check with a top-down still at f1249 against S11 f1152.

fixes.area: light (chiaroscuro / torso competes with face)
fixes.problem: The treatment asks for chiaroscuro: a hard top light carving the head, with darkness everywhere else. Measured linear luminance from f1249 to f1320: head-top p90 is 0.52 and breastplate p90 is 0.28-0.30, under 1 stop apart, and the medians are about equal. So a large lit ochre breastplate with the saturated blue chip fills the bottom 25% of every frame and pulls the eye off the LED face. The plates sit in the mid-tones, so they read mustard rather than the ivory they read as in S05/S11 (S05 head top sRGB 225/214/201 against 200/178/155 here). Only after f1330, when the slab edge leaves his right side, does the frame become chiaroscuro. f1344 is the best still in the shot, which shows the gap.
fixes.fix: Take the breastplate down about 2 stops (torso p90 <= ~0.12 linear) and leave the head key, right forearm, hand and cup alone. Either use a camera-invisible, shadow-only flag card above the chest that cuts the room sun off the breastplate below the collar (it must stay clear of rays to the head face and the cup at the chin), or use an object-index or ID-mask compositor grade on the torso plates. Then consider raising EXPOSURE from -0.3 toward 0 so the crown's top facets reach ivory. Keep the slab-edge slide across the forearm, elbow and head cone readable.

fixes.area: continuity: headset rest (S11 -> S13 -> S14)
fixes.problem: s13_first_sip.py headset_on_walnut places the headset at its own spot: (0.34, -0.12, 0.9) with a -90 deg turn about Y, then snaps it to the table. It does not use the pose S11 exports for exactly this hand-over: s11_shutdown.HEADSET_REST = ((0.3, -0.25, 0.8221), (0.70182, -0.0867, -0.08595, 0.70182)). A build of S11 confirms that pose at f1150/f1152. Measured headset bbox centre: S11 f1152 (0.281, -0.244, 0.858); S13 f1249 (0.301, -0.110, 0.986). That is 13.4 cm closer to him, 12.8 cm higher, and resting on a different face. The headset is off screen in S13, but S14 copies S13's pose plus the 3.5 cm slide (verified identical at f1345). So the prop visibly jumps and turns between S11's set-down beside the hub and S14's top-down f1345-1356, where it is in frame. Both placements are physically valid (lowest vertex +0.5 mm / +0.4 mm above the walnut, no BVH overlap with hub, padlock, socket or cord). They just disagree.
fixes.fix: In headset_on_walnut, key hs.location and hs.rotation_quaternion at START-10 from S11's HEADSET_REST, either by importing s11_shutdown.HEADSET_REST or by copying the constant with a comment. Drop the zmin re-snap: S11's rest is already 0.4 mm above the walnut. Apply the HEADSET_DX slide from that rest; +X moves away from the hub. Make the same change in s14_circle_back.headset_on_walnut (rest + 0.035 m in X). Then re-run a BVH overlap of the slid headset against hub_body, padlock_kevin_*, master cord and socket at f1334-1344.

fixes.area: performance: hand rise f1121-1128 (headset_off, rise_keys, s11_shutdown.py ~546-563)
fixes.problem: Every beat lands on its treatment frame, but the left hand is not deadpan or mechanical here. Probe of world positions: the hand covers 1.07 m in 5 frames (f1121-1126) at 4.4/5.5/4.8/6.0/5.0 m/s, which is punch speed. It overshoots above the band to z 1.772 at f1127, then drops 6 cm onto it at f1129. The proof at f1124 shows a blurred ivory smear swinging out past the pauldron. It reads as a swat, not a precise servo reach.
fixes.fix: Use all 8 treatment frames: rise_keys = (1120, pa), (1124, w1), (1128, w2), (1129, pb). Cut the w1 detour (+0.24 m in x) to the minimum that clears the pauldron. Approach the band from the side at its own height: drop the +0.35 z tilt of out_n and HS['approach'] up-and-out, so the hand never rises above the grip point. Prefer two eased straight segments with a 1-frame hold at w1 (servo move, stop, move) over the Catmull-Rom swoop. Target a peak of 2.5 m/s or less. Re-run S11_DEBUG report() for arm clearances.

fixes.area: performance: headset turn and set-down f1136-1150 (HS['lift'] lines 296-298, delta()/_hermite)
fixes.problem: The lift itself is good: 10 cm at about 0.5 m/s, f1130-1135. After that the headset whips 75° about the vertical in 5 frames (1.35-2.15 m/s, f1136-1140). The Catmull-Rom tangent carries that speed through f1140 into a 0.8 m plunge to the walnut peaking at 2.9 m/s (f1144-1145). That is 15 continuous frames at 2-3 m/s, which reads as yank and drop. Proof frames f1140 and f1145 are blurred smears of hand and arm.
fixes.fix: Keep the treatment landmarks (10 cm up by f1135, on the walnut with the parent swap at f1150) and make f1136-1150 one deliberate move. Spread the 75-90° yaw across f1136-1150 instead of f1136-1140, don't let the grip rise during the turn, and give LIFT_END a zero tangent (or drop it as a key) so the set-down is a single eased, near-straight line. Target a peak of about 1.5 m/s. Re-check the right earcup's clearance past the face with report().

fixes.area: framing: frame-top contact f1136-1139
fixes.problem: At f1138 Synergy_palm_L reaches z 1.855 and touches the top edge of the frame (ray-cast hit at image y 0.01; lit pixel in row 0 of the proof). The debug report has headset vertices at 0.986-0.996 of frame height for f1137-1139. The 75° turn adds 4.4 cm of rise (palm z 1.795 at f1135 to 1.839 at f1138). A hand cropped by the frame edge is not a printable still.
fixes.fix: Hold the grip at or below its f1135 height through the turn (see the previous fix). Add a gate to report(): the highest image point of palm, fingers and headset stays at or below 0.95 of frame height (at least 45 px of headroom at 900) on every frame f1121-1150. If the band can't clear the crown under that cap, move it out to +X before up.

fixes.area: readability: the black headset vanishes against the black room
fixes.problem: The film's last action in the room, the headset coming off and being set down, has no visible prop. At f1145 a 28 px window round the headset averages 0.032 luma (p90 0.054). At f1135-1140 only a hairline of band shows, so the action reads as 'arm swings over head'; only the bare head afterwards tells you what happened. In the final still f1152 the headset is two dark circles by the dark hub.
fixes.fix: Add a small light, light-linked to the headset and its children only, on the slab side (above and front-left of the head, out of the lens's view). Key it on from f1128 to the end so the band's top edge and the earcup shells carry a thin specular line through the lift and at rest. Alternatively, add the headset to a receiver set for a glancing slab-coloured spot. Target headset edges of 0.15 luma or more against black at f1135-1150, and an unmistakable headset silhouette at f1152. Keep visible_camera off.

fixes.area: light: terminal rim cards (terminal_rims, RIM, s11_shutdown.py 664-708)
fixes.problem: 1) The rim cards ignore distance: E = 26*sqrt(6/d). The probe reads Linda (23 m) at 13-17 W and People (18 m) at about 20 W at their flares, against Synthia's 26 W at 3 m; inverse-square gives Linda about 1/60 of Synthia. So at f1025-1041 his head, earcup, neck and left arm carry a saturated magenta-red rim (442 px with saturation above 0.3 at f1036), the most saturated thing in frame. Its source is a speck hidden in the vanishing-point stack, so the flash seems to come from beside him and the wave doesn't recede. 2) All nine cards have visible_glossy on. When Pat powers on, the 0.7 m card mirrors in the enamel: the probe names the plate head_cheek_l_low, and that pixel jumps from 0.056 to 0.93 luma, the brightest point on him, from 'a soft grey glow 23 m away'. The A/B render with rim glossy off removes the streak (head max 0.93 to 0.82; pixels above 0.6 drop from 1168 to 899).
fixes.fix: Use E = RIM['energy'] * min(1, (3.0/d)**2), or at least 1/d with a low floor, so the far colleagues' flashes are whispers and the colour visibly drains near to far. Set lt.visible_glossy = False on every rim card. The real screens already reflect in the glass and enamel, and the cards only exist to light diffusely. Drop RIM['pat'] from 12 to about 1-2 W, so Pat's arrival is a faint grey breath on his edge rather than a lamp switched on next to him.

fixes.area: continuity: HEADSET_REST is not used by S13/S14
fixes.problem: S11 leaves the headset at (0.30, -0.25, 0.822) standing on its earcups, yawed 90° (earcups in line down the table), and prints HEADSET_REST for S13 and S14. Both shots ignore it. s13_first_sip.py headset_on_walnut (line 274) and s14_circle_back.py headset_on_walnut (line 329) hard-code (0.34, -0.12) rotated -90° about Y, which lays it on its side; S14 adds +3.5 cm. S14's top-down f1345 explicitly shows the headset beside the hub, so it won't match S11's last frame.
fixes.fix: S13 and S14 should import s11_shutdown.HEADSET_REST (location and quaternion) as their start pose and apply S13's slide from there; their owners make that edit. S11 already prints and checks the value; keep it authoritative.

fixes.area: Headset take-off: left-arm IK pops (f1121-1150), s11_shutdown.py _solve_hand / headset_off
fixes.problem: _solve_hand re-runs rig.solve_arm_clear on every frame and picks the elbow pole and shoulder from discrete candidate sets (GRIP_SHOULDERS steps 4-10 deg, poles at ±0.35 offsets). The prefer() continuity weight (0.6·pole + 0.004·deg) is too weak, so the solution jumps between frames. Per-frame bone data (crit1-tech/anim/arm.json): upperarm_L turns 96.8 deg/frame at f1125 and 114.3 deg/frame at f1145, where the elbow moves 236 mm in one frame against 123 mm for the wrist. The arm goes from bent to straight between f1136 and f1137. shoulder_L and pauldron_L jitter on alternate frames: 0 / 8.5 / 0 / 8.2 / 0.5 / 12.8 / 24.1 deg from f1129 to f1135, the pauldron moves 48 deg/frame at f1135 and 40 at f1137, and the shoulder 39.8 at f1141 and 40.2 at f1144. This is clearly visible in the every-frame animatic: crit1-tech/pops_lift.png and headset_every.png show the arm hanging at f1124, a straight diagonal at f1125 and vertical at f1126, plus the pauldron flips at f1137 and f1145. With motion blur at proof quality the frames become smeared streaks (arm_zoom_a.png, zoom_b.png). This is the shot's hero action, and it is exactly the cheap-looking hand contact the treatment's risk list warns about.
fixes.fix: Stop searching on every frame. Solve only the key poses: the f1120 hold, f1124, GRIP 1129, 1132, LIFT_UP 1135, LIFT_END 1140, 1145 and SET 1150. In each segment, interpolate the shoulder angles and the elbow pole vector continuously (lerp the shoulder, slerp the pole) between the key solutions. On the in-between frames, re-solve only the wrist with that fixed pole and shoulder, and keep the clearance search for the key frames. Alternatively, limit the per-frame candidates to the previous pole and shoulder ±2 deg and raise the continuity weight by about 100x. Then call rig.bake_pauldrons(RISE[0], END+2). Add a gate to report(): no left-arm bone over 15 deg/frame and no frame where the elbow moves more than 1.5x the wrist. Re-check with an every-frame animatic over f1119-1152.

fixes.area: Hand rise speed (f1121-1128)
fixes.problem: The hand covers about 1 m in 5 frames. Hand-bone speed is 64 mm at f1121 (a 6.4 cm first-frame jump with no ease-in), then 156, 194, 183, 243 (f1125: 5.8 m/s), 210, 52 and 60 mm/frame. The near-stop at the w2 waypoint (GRIP-3) is a 177 mm/frame² deceleration in one frame. On a deadpan robot this reads as a whip, and at proof and final quality it renders as a motion-blur smear (r0/1124.png). The +24 cm outward detour w1 makes the path about 25% longer than it needs to be.
fixes.fix: Shrink the w1 detour to the minimum the clearance solver accepts (about 8 cm) and use one eased C1 curve over f1121-1129, with the approach waypoint at f1127 instead of f1126 so the deceleration is spread out. Aim for a peak of 150 mm/frame or less and a first-frame move under 2 cm. If clearance makes that impossible inside the treatment's 8 frames, tell the director that an 8-frame rise from the table edge to the earcup cannot read as calm.

fixes.area: Continuity S11 -> S13/S14: headset rest
fixes.problem: S11 solves and prints HEADSET_REST = (0.30, -0.25, 0.8221), q(0.70182, -0.0867, -0.08595, 0.70182), and verified it numerically: headset 0.4 mm above the walnut, still from f1150. The docstring says this is 'for S13/S14', but neither script uses it. s13_first_sip.headset_on_walnut and s14_circle_back.headset_on_walnut hard-code (0.34, -0.12) rotated -90 deg about Y; S14 adds +3.5 cm. That is 13-14 cm away from S11's rest and about 112 deg different in orientation. S14's top-down shot (f1345-1356) shows the headset in a different place, sitting over Kevin's padlock, which S11's rest search keeps 25 mm clear (s14/p2/s14/1345.png; crit1-tech/s14_1345_headedge_x4.png).
fixes.fix: In S13 and S14, `from s11_shutdown import HEADSET_REST` and key the headset empty to it at the same frames they key it now. Keep S13's downhill slide as a world-space offset from that rest. Optionally have S11 write the rest to a small JSON file so S13 and S14 don't need to import S11's build code. Re-render S14 at f1345 to confirm.

fixes.area: Eclipse silhouette f106-128: reads as a UI toggle-switch icon, not as fingers
fixes.problem: Renders are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-linkedin/35346f8e-3086-50e0-b336-b295d0b54106/scratchpad/shots/s01/crit1-cine/ (proof/s01, end.png, crops.png, anim_end.png). At f108-f112 a perfect dark disc appears inside the right end of the flat white pill. At f116-f120 that dark 'knob' slides along the pill. At the rest frame f124-f128 (the match-cut frame) the result is a black pill with a round lobe at its right end, set off by the notch waist, plus a small grey nub just outside the rim. That is the iOS on/off toggle icon, an accidental pictogram in a film with no glyphs. The treatment's 'fingertips pinching the edge of a folded envelope' never reads, so the cut cannot make 'the occluding silhouette become the real fingers'. Causes: (a) eclipse_outline() is the slot inset by 1.5 m, so the leading edge is the slot's own semicircular cap, concentric with it; (b) the two notches (x = +18 and +24 m after the half turn) sit almost opposite each other and pinch a waist, leaving a near-circular lobe about 45 m wide; (c) the uncovered slot is a flat clipped white with almost no halation, so it reads as a graphic pill, not a sun; (d) HAND_SHADE is two soft boxes, so the lid only darkens as a shapeless gradient and no hand reads anywhere in the frame.
fixes.fix: Do this inside the shot: build_eclipse is owned by the library, so replace or add the rig's child geometry in stage_eclipse. (1) Lead with the envelope's straight folded edge, slanted about 20-30 degrees off vertical, or with its corner. The first dark shape inside the slot must be a straight diagonal, never a disc. (2) Replace the opposed notch pair with unequal, offset pads: the index pad on the top edge and the thumb pad on the bottom edge, 25-35 m apart along X, with different radii. They may just break the rim, so the outline is organic and asymmetric, with no waist and no round end lobe. (3) Turn the lid shade into a soft but legible thumb-and-index silhouette on the backlit vault, like a shadow puppet behind paper, readable from about f110. It should converge on the slot from the lower right, toward the rim: after the cut's vertical flip, that is where S02's fingers enter, upper right. (4) Give the uncovered slot a sun's warm halation on the vault (f96-f112) that falls away with the eclipse, so it reads as light. Re-measure the cut afterwards. Today S01's silhouette is 0.179 W x 0.084 H with its centre at 0.498/0.498, and S02 f129's slot is 0.179-0.181 W x 0.093 H with its centre at 0.498-0.500/0.505: keep at least that agreement.

fixes.area: Arch f14-f104: the padlocks are already legible
fixes.problem: The treatment says 'The arch reads only as a silhouette; its padlocks are not yet legible.' On the 800 px proof (c50.png) you can pick out shackle hooks all along both legs and blocky padlock bodies, and the scree at the feet glints as recognisable padlocks. At the 1600 px final they will read more clearly. This gives away S06's reveal of the arch of six hundred padlocks, and the arch's flat black, unhazed cut-out also flattens the depth between it and the cliff.
fixes.fix: Change S01 only. Lower the fills for padlock and arch_stone from the framing's 0.3 and 0.35 to about 0.05-0.1. Cut the warm key's gold glints off the arch and the scree, either with apply_light_levels on the key or by keeping the key's glossy contribution off the arch. Add a few per cent of haze on the arch so its outline softens into a single mass. Then check a --quality final crop of f50: no shackle or padlock body should be identifiable.

fixes.area: Glide f20-f80: barely reads as forward travel
fixes.problem: Over 60 frames the camera covers 7.5 m toward a world about 240 m away. The arch's size and position on screen do not change measurably (the wall differs by 0.005 mean between f41 and f49), so f20, f50 and f80 are practically the same still. The only cue of travel is one lens floe about every 14 frames. The treatment's 'low forward glide' plays as a locked-off shot with debris drifting through it.
fixes.fix: Keep 3 m/s and the approved framing, but add continuous near-field cues within 2-10 m of the lens. Stream crema lace, bubble specks or fine foam streaks on the water under the lens. Add more, smaller floes (one every 4-6 frames), including some near the left and right frame edges for parallax. Strengthen the capillary flow on the water near the lens so it slides toward camera. Check the result on a step-2 animatic of f20-80.

fixes.area: Match-cut frame f112-128: the shaft prism shows through the slot
fixes.problem: env_offline.build_shaft starts the beam prism on the plane through SLOT_C that is perpendicular to SHAFT_DIR. That plane sits 18.5 deg off the lid's slot plane (perpendicular to SLOT_N), so on one side the prism's top pokes about 10-20 m out through the hole. From the S01 lens it puts a grey film over the silhouette's right lobe and a hard-edged grey crescent with a doubled edge at the slot's right end. This shows from f112 and through the f124-128 hold, so the rim at the cut is not even. Ray casts at f128 inside the hole hit OFF_Shaft 5-13 m beyond the slot plane. Hiding the shaft from camera removes the artifact completely: luminance of the inside right lobe drops from 28.7 to 9.8 (final crops). Evidence: crit1-tech/measure/noshaft_compare2x.png and shaftclip_compare2x.png; final crops in crit1-tech/final_crop/.
fixes.fix: Shot-side, until the library changes: after build, add to h['mats']['shaft'] a TexCoord(object=h['objects']['slot_frame']) -> SeparateXYZ.Z -> MapRange (SMOOTHSTEP, from -20 to 0 => 1 to 0) node chain, and multiply its result into the Emission node's Strength. Tested at final on f104, f116 and f128: the crescent and the film are gone, the ghost shaft stays, and the beam still leaves the slot at f104 (test script: crit1-tech/probe/lidfix.py mode shaftclip). Report to the env_offline owner: build the prism's first ring on the slot plane (project the cap points along SHAFT_DIR onto the plane perpendicular to SLOT_N through SLOT_C) and measure 'head' from there. Any shot that sees the slot (S06, S08) has the same problem.

fixes.area: Lens floes f9-88: dark 'sunburst' on every floe
fixes.problem: Every crema floe shows a ring of dark radial wedges round its centre. The lens floes are 150-250 px wide at 1600 px, for example the bottom-centre floe at f40 (crit1-tech/measure/f40_final_floes.png). Root cause is in env_offline._floe_blob: the centre-fan triangles are wound counter-clockwise (normal +Z), but the ring quads from grid_faces are wound the other way (normal -Z). Only 28,272 of 92,852 floe faces face up. Smooth shading averages opposite normals at the first ring, which produces the wedges. Ray casts confirm it: the quads are back-facing. It is not holes or interpenetration: filling the holes or flattening the pieces changed nothing.
fixes.fix: Shot-side workaround (tested at final on f40, sunburst gone: crit1-tech/measure/floefix3_compare.png): after build_offline, run bmesh on h['objects']['floes'].data: bmesh.ops.recalc_face_normals(bm, faces=bm.faces), then normal_flip() every face with normal.z < 0, then to_mesh. Library fix for the env_offline owner: reverse the quad winding in _floe_blob (fq = fq[:, ::-1]). The floes in S06, S08, S12 and S14 have the same bug.

fixes.area: S01 f128 -> S02 f129 match cut: size and vertical position
fixes.problem: Both frames measured at proof (800 px) with the same threshold. S01 f128: dark silhouette 19.0% of width, centre (0.499, 0.499); bright outline 20.5%; geometric slot 20.0%. S02 f129: dark slot 17.6-17.9%, centre (0.501, 0.504). So S02's slot is about 6% narrower than S01's dark shape and about 10% narrower than S01's slot, and it sits 0.0055 of the frame height lower (about 5 px at 1600x900). The S01 docstring says S02's slot edge lands on S01's bright rim. That is false: it lands about 4 px (at 800) inside the silhouette at each end. Orientation matches: long axis within 1 deg, lid centre flips top/bottom as documented, fingers at frame right in both. The treatment requires the same size. Evidence: crit1-tech/cut_pair.jpg, cut_overlay_zoom.png (red = S01, cyan = S02), cut_blend.png.
fixes.fix: Agree one target with the S02 owner. Preferred: S02 D0 from 0.208 to about 0.196 m, so its dark slot reads about 19% like S01's silhouette, and raise S02's framing by about 0.005 of frame height. S01-only alternative: END_LOC, END_LENS = E.slot_match_camera(frac=0.188) (about 41.1 mm), so S01's silhouette is about 17.9%, plus keying cam.data.shift_y to about +0.003 through the settle so the slot sits 5 px lower. Re-measure both frames with crit1-tech/measure/blob.py (dark < 0.2) and aim for under 2% width and under 2 px difference.

fixes.area: Camera move f560-608 (pacing, reveal, printable stills)
fixes.problem: The +8.3 to +67.5 deg tilt and the 67 m push are packed into about f572-600 by C.ease(t**1.2). Report values give a peak of 2.4 deg/frame (58 deg/s) and a push of about 2.8 m/frame (66 m/s), so the 22.9 deg vertical FOV is crossed in under 10 frames: a whip-tilt, not a reveal. Frames f575-f596 are motion smears: Sobel edge energy is 3.1 at f588 against 7.0 at rest (f608). f585, f588 and f594 are about 60% empty paper wall with one smeared diagonal leg. The treatment's payoff is the ageing gradient read 'as we tilt' (brass, patina, verdigris, lichen), and it passes at peak speed, so it never reads. The move is still turning at f606-608, so the payoff composition gets no hold before the f609 cut. A 240 km/h dolly past 11 m padlocks is also a miniature tell. The hero slides out of frame at about f577, before its f578 settle. Evidence: crit1-cine/anim_sheet.jpg, proof/s06/0578.png, 0588.png, proof2/s06/0575.png, 0594.png (all under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-linkedin/35346f8e-3086-50e0-b336-b295d0b54106/scratchpad/shots/s06/).
fixes.fix: Replace C.ease(t**MOVE_WARP) in Move.u with a linear-cruise profile: an 8-10 frame ease-in, constant speed, and a 10-12 frame ease-out landing by about f598, then hold at rest f598-608 so the slot-in-arch frame reads before the cut. Start the move as the hop lands (f556-558 if the director accepts a 2-4 frame shift; otherwise keep f560) so the slow start doesn't eat 10 frames. Cap the peak at about 7% of the vertical FOV per frame. Start the push closer (about 85-95 m from the arch on the same landing line, not 121 m) so the reveal is mostly tilt, not dolly. Keep the settled hero in frame until about f580. Check with an every-2nd-frame animatic over f556-608.

fixes.area: Lens and payoff framing (needs a director decision)
fixes.problem: At 50 mm the end frame (env 's06_arch', 55 m out) is a worm's-eye view through a ring. Both legs are cropped at the sides and the crest at the top, so the audience never sees 'the whole 110 m arch' the treatment's reveal promises. The blown white slot inside the grey lid-ring ellipse reads as a ceiling lamp seen through a doughnut. A probe with the shot's own camera keys and only the lens changed to 35 mm (crit1-cine/lens35/s06/0608.png) shows both legs, the crest, and the slot inside the opening under the ribbed dome: a readable arch. At f553 (lens35/s06/0553.png) it also adds the espresso sea with its gold glitter path and the cliff's height, both asked for in the treatment's Light section and cropped out at 50 mm. The 50 mm lens also forces the near-60 deg tilt above.
fixes.fix: Propose 35 mm for S06 to the director, alongside the cup-world lens changes already accepted (S01 19 mm, S08 14 mm, S12 30 mm, S14 18 mm). If approved, re-pick the opening pitch so the landing sits in the lower third with the falling padlock still large enough to read. Re-solve the end pitch so the slot sits in the upper half of the opening. The required tilt shrinks and its speed relative to the frame drops by about 30%, which compounds with the cruise-profile fix. If 50 mm must stay, test ending 10-20 m further out to get both legs' inner edges into frame, confirming the slot stays inside the opening.

fixes.area: Hero padlock tumble: identity lost on the flash frames, scale tell
fixes.problem: SPIN = 45 deg/frame is 3.0 rev/s; the comment says 1.9 rev/s, which is wrong. For an 11 m 'three-storey' body that is about 100 m/s at the tips, a classic miniature giveaway. The half-frame shutter smears the shackle exactly on the flash frames. At final quality f548 (crit1-cine/final/crop_0548.png) the padlock reads as a cream slab with a translucent half-disc fan, not a padlock. The off-flash frames f546 and f550 read crisply (crops/flash_strip.png). So the object is unrecognisable on precisely the beats designed to feature it.
fixes.fix: Re-key retumble() at 15 deg/frame or less (1 rev/s), nearer 8-10 if the flashes allow. Get the three treatment flashes from three different surfaces crossing the glint direction (broad face, shackle crown, opposite face or bevel), or from a second glossy-only glint disc, rather than from three half-turns. Verify at final with motion blur that the shackle stays a solid U on every flash frame.

fixes.area: Flash colour (treatment: 'flashes gold')
fixes.problem: Measured on proof f544 and f548, the top 3% of hero pixels sit at hue 27-28 deg, saturation 0.17, value 0.97-0.98: pale peach-cream. A gold reference (#ffd17a) is hue 39 deg, saturation 0.52. At final, f548's face reads as soap, not brass. GLINT_L = 12 at GLINT_K = 3600 overexposes the face, and AgX desaturates it toward white, despite the comment claiming it stays gold.
fixes.fix: Lower GLINT_L to about 5-6 and GLINT_K to 2800-3000 (or tint the disc toward #ffc060). Target a flash face around 0.8-0.85 display luma with saturation of 0.4 or more and hue 35-45 deg, measured at final. Keep the flash brighter than its neighbours (today p95 luma alternates 226/157/229/75/228 over f544-552, which is the right cadence).

fixes.area: Bounce physics f553-566 (scale)
fixes.problem: animate_hero_padlock keys a 3.2 m hop apex over the 13-frame bounce: 8 x 3.2 / (13/24)^2 = 87 m/s^2, about 9 g. In f556-559 the padlock floats horizontally several metres above the scree like a flicked toy. At real gravity a 13-frame hop rises only 0.36 m. Gravity is what sells size; the fall itself is keyed at real g, so the hop contradicts it.
fixes.fix: Re-key the f554-566 segment in the shot after the env call, as retumble() already does for the fall. Make it a heavy bite: a heave of 0.5 m or less plus a rock about its leading edge (tip about 10-15 deg and fall back) on f553-566, then the slide to settle on f567-578, keeping the treatment frames. Keep the dust on f554. Report to the Offline owner that the hop height (lift = 3.2) should be a parameter of animate_hero_padlock.

fixes.area: Cut-in and fall timing f529-552
fixes.problem: After the hard cut that is meant to be 'following the padlock in', f529-541 are 13 frames (0.55 s) of a static leg with nothing moving. The shackle first breaks the top edge at f542 (proof2/s06/0542.png), so the whole fall is on screen for about 10 frames (0.4 s): too short to read the tumble, the three flashes and the size. The flashes on f544/548/552 each sit one frame ahead of the 16th-note grid (545/549/553); beat 34 starts at f545.
fixes.fix: Lower IMPACT from 62 to about 32-38 m/s, still at real g. The drop then reads slower and bigger, and the padlock breaks the top edge by about f533-537, giving 16-20 frames of fall. Put the flashes on the grid at f541, f545 (the beat-34 downbeat) and f549, with the impact on f553. Re-run env's arch-clearance check; animate_hero_padlock re-solves the start candidates.

fixes.area: Crest look: lichen and age read (env-owned, report to Offline)
fixes.problem: The treatment's oldest padlocks are 'crusted with chartreuse #e5ff8d and frost-grey lichen'. In final f608 (crit1-cine/final/s06/0608.png), chartreuse covers 0.01% of pixels. The crest reads as charcoal terrazzo with an even polka-dot print of grey dots and pin-point yellow cores, not crust. The undersides of the stone-age padlocks, lit by warm bounce, read as brown cardboard. In the mid-tilt frames (f585) the patina transition is a teal-and-brown camouflage patchwork.
fixes.fix: Report to the env_offline owner (mat_padlock, stone stage): fewer, larger, irregular clumped rosettes with clear chartreuse cores, thicker coverage on top faces and toward the crest, varied size and density so it stops reading as a print. If the owner can't turn it round, override in-shot the way soften_puddles() and glow_dust() do (lichen threshold and colour nodes) and verify at final f608.

fixes.area: Payoff has no scale cue; pines missing
fixes.problem: The treatment tops the arch with 'a fringe of small pines', its own device for reading 110 m. The shot drops them because they sit on the crest's top face, out of sight from below. The end frame then has no scale reference: no pines, no haze on the arch, nothing small. Together with the crisp lid ring it reads as a tabletop arch under a lamp.
fixes.fix: In-shot, let 8-15 pine tips break the crest's outer silhouette against the lid in the end frame. Use instances from env pine_templates along the visible crest rim, or nudge the existing crest pines nearest the edge outward. Check at final that they read as tiny trees, not fuzz. A wider end lens (fix 2) makes them read more easily.

fixes.area: Hero padlock settle: a pop and the padlock passing through the scree (f564-571)
fixes.problem: I sampled the hero padlock's keys at quarter frames and tested them against the scree and arch BVHs. The env's _lift_clear keeps the padlock on top of loose scree padlocks until f570 (centre z 11.0 m, 1.2-1.6 m above the mound). On f571 it drops 1.3 m in a single frame to its bedded rest (z 9.7, 0.3 m into the mound). In the proofs that is about 18 px of its own motion at 800 px, roughly 36 px at final, after four frames of nearly level sliding. The linear interpolation between those keys cuts through scree padlocks at subframes 570.25 and 570.75 (18 and 20 overlapping triangle pairs). That falls inside the shutters of f570 and f571, and final/s06/0571.png shows a vertical ghost of the body and shackle over the scree. The hop also touches down early: z reaches 11.5 on f564, holds through f565, then rises 0.1 m on f566, so the BOUNCE sync point (f566) never reads as a contact. The arch itself is clear on every frame and subframe, and so is the fall (f529-553).
fixes.fix: Do this inside s06 after animate_hero_padlock() and retumble(). Re-solve the ground keys f554-578 on quarter-frame samples. Take z_req(t) as the _lift_clear height against E._scree_bvh(arch, land, rest, radius>=40), and build z(t) = max(z_req, a slope-limited envelope): one forward and one backward pass, with |dz| no more than about 0.3 m per frame. That turns the 1.3 m step into an eased slide-off over about f569-575. Build the hop on lerp(z_land, z_req(566), t) + 3.2*4t(1-t) so it touches down exactly on f566. Keep the f578 pose identical to the current rest (z 9.7): s08_landscape.py calls animate_hero_padlock() and holds that pose, so this keeps S08 continuity. Key every frame, then assert zero scree and arch overlaps at f-0.25, f and f+0.25 for f553-578.

fixes.area: Tilt speed: heavy motion blur, and frames that do not hold as stills (f574-600)
fixes.problem: The measured turn rate peaks at 2.53 deg/frame on f588. The docstring says 2.4. At 50 mm on a 1600 px frame that is about 98 px of motion per frame and about 49 px of blur at the 0.5 shutter. Frames f574-f600 (27 of the shot's 80) carry more than 20 px of blur. The proof frames proof/s06/0578.png and 0588.png are diagonal smears of the leg, not stills worth printing. The treatment's 25->55 deg move peaks near 1.2 deg/frame. The documented deviation (+8.3 -> +67.5 deg pitch plus a 67 m push, all inside f560-608, shaped by smootherstep on t**1.2 with a peak of about 1.9x the average) doubles it. Noise handling during the move is correct. The seed is fixed through f562 (motion 1.3 px/frame or less), animated f563-607 and fixed on f608, so no noise sticks to the screen.
