fixes.fix: Replace C.ease(t**MOVE_WARP) with a trapezoidal velocity profile: accelerate f560-574, cruise, decelerate f590-608 into the slot. That gives a peak of about 1.8 deg/frame. For a further cut, start the opening frame 3-4 deg higher (the f553 landing still clears the bottom edge at y of about 0.05-0.25), and/or key render.motion_blur_shutter down to about 0.3 over f576-598. Target: blur no more than about 25 px at final on every frame. Check with proof renders of f580, f588 and f596 and an animatic strip of f576-600.

fixes.area: Continuity with S04/S05: Kevin's padlock has a steel shackle in the room, a brass one in Offline
fixes.problem: In the room, props.padlock() gives Kevin's padlock a silver hardened-steel shackle (shackle_steel), and it reads clearly in S05 (s05 proof f479). The Offline hero is E.padlock_template(variant 0) with a single mat_padlock(age=0.03), so its shackle is brass like the body. You can see this in proof/s06/0544.png and final/s06/0571.png. The proportions do match: body W/H is 1.19 in both, the shackle rises about 0.8 of the body height, and the wire is about 0.09 of the body height. So the shackle colour is the one cue that breaks 'same padlock'. S09 brings the steel-shackled padlock back.
fixes.fix: Inside s06, after build_offline: append a steel material slot to h['objects']['hero_padlock']. Use metallic 1, base about (0.6, 0.6, 0.58), roughness about 0.22, and reuse the pits/scratch bump if possible. Set material_index=1 on the shackle polygons: the faces after the body box, whose count is len(E._rounded_box(0.31, 0.13, 0.26, 0.07, n=12)[1]), through the tube and its two caps. Leave the collars brass, as on the room prop. Report it to the env_offline owner so build_hero_padlock() does the same for S08, which shows the padlock at rest.

fixes.area: performance: envelope-to-bird unfold (f772-790)
fixes.problem: The film's key transformation never reads as folding. The envelope is a 7-vertex fan blended straight into the 7-vertex bird. At delivery resolution it goes from a flat card (f772) to a flat white pentagon with a blue square (f776, f779) to an edge-on rhombus (f784), then becomes a paper dart (f790). There are no flaps, creases or wings opening. An ILM supervisor would read this as a polygon tween, not paper. Evidence: crit1-cine/probe/envcrop_sheet.png (1600 px crops, final quality).
fixes.fix: Give the shot its own hinged envelope mesh, about 12-16 vertices: a body diamond plus top, bottom and two side flaps, written to the same s08 pc2. Animate rigid rotations about the crease lines rather than a vertex lerp. f768-774: the top flap lifts and becomes the head and tail. f772-784: the side flaps swing out 0 to 150 degrees and become the wings, then join the WINGBEAT flap. Use flat-shaded facets so alternate folds catch the beam light and the fill. Fold the seal under the closing body by about f780 instead of shrinking it in place. Keep the beat-48 face-on pose on f769 and the f772 unfold sound sync.

fixes.area: cinematography: hero legibility on beat 48 (f766-772)
fixes.problem: On the beat-48 'face-on, seal showing' frame the hero is a soft smear. The crane pull-back adds to the fall, so on screen the card moves 92 px/frame (f760-764) and 55 px/frame (f764-768) at 1600 px. At a 0.5 shutter that blurs about 25 px across a 130-170 px card, and the seal smears into a vertical streak (envcrop 0766, 0769). The card is also the same value as what sits behind it, the beam and the paper wall (card about RGB 231,220,211; wall about 226,220,215 at f768). It is parked between the two brightest whites in frame (the shaft and the falls), so the eye has to hunt for it. The seal reads periwinkle (166,179,226), not cobalt #0757ec.
fixes.fix: Re-time envelope_path so the card catches air and hangs. Bring the deceleration forward so screen speed is under 10 px/frame over f767-771, with a flutter-swing apex on f769, and let it drop and slide again after the unfold. Alternatively give the crane a slow passage at f766-772 instead of its peak speed at the cut. Move ENV_FRAME's target off the beam and falls, e.g. ENV_X_OFF negative into the darker mid-wall left of the shaft, or ENV_Y lower against the darker lower cliff, so white sits on a field at least 25% darker. Rebalance ENV_SUN and ENV_FILL so the lens-facing side is brighter than the wall without washing out the seal. Check the seal reads as cobalt at final quality.

fixes.area: hero prop: the seal turns black (f772)
fixes.problem: When the tumble shows the face away from both light-linked lamps, the opaque principled cobalt seal drops to near-black with an orange fringe. It reads as a burn hole or printed mark on the card (proof 0772 crop; envcrop 0772). It is not text, but it is an artefact on the hero.
fixes.fix: Give the seal what the paper already has: a little translucency or a small emission floor in the shot's own seal material, or a fill lamp linked to it from the lens side. Or adjust the ENV_FACE and TUMBLE phase so the seal's lit face is the one toward the lens whenever the seal is visible (f764-778).

fixes.area: murmuration: bird colour and continuity with the hero bird
fixes.problem: The treatment calls for white origami birds with glowing edges. The flock renders as brown and black specks, and the near strays as 20-40 px brown triangles, which read as moths, soot or bats (crops/0790_strays.png, final 0832). Because the hero bird has its own linked lamps, it is the only white bird in the frame. The beat 'it joins a murmuration of thousands of them' fails: it visibly does not match them. From f785 to f801 the brown strays are also larger and stronger than the hero, so they pull the eye away from it.
fixes.fix: In the shot, call apply_values(h, {'bird': {'BirdEdgeGlow': 3-4}}). Add a soft front fill from behind the lens, light-linked to the murmuration, near-stray and roost objects only (the same pattern as envelope_lights), so their faces read as shaded white paper at about 0.6-0.8 of the wall value with bright rims, not 0.3. Then match the hero bird's linked lamps to that look so it disappears into the flock by f832. If the env owner wants the dark-cored ribbon kept, raise it with them; as rendered, it contradicts the treatment.

fixes.area: story legibility: the ring atoll
fixes.problem: From the approved 10 m lens the atoll is about 470 m away. The 150 m ring is foreshortened to about 4 px, so all that reads is a strip of palms on the horizon, which looks like mangroves (final 0832 crop, envcrop 0784-0801). The glowing caramel lagoon is invisible. The 'glass zero carried forward' payoff, one of only four landforms and the setup for Linda's zero in S07, is lost.
fixes.fix: Keep the approved framing and make the ring read through light. In the shot, apply_values(h, {'sea': {'LagoonGlow': about 2-3}}) so a caramel band glows between the palm groves and reflects in the near water. Check that the ivory inner beach catches the beam. If it still reads as a line, ask the Offline owner to thin the near-side palms on the atoll so the lagoon glow shows through the gap.

fixes.area: light and colour: golden afternoon and the attendee blooms
fixes.problem: The poster is monochrome tan. Sampled wall hue is 23-33 degrees at saturation 0.10-0.45 across the frame, so it reads as cardboard rather than gold. Of the eight blooms, only Operations orange (right edge) and a faint People pink behind the arch read. Keys cobalt and Strategy acid yellow project to x 0.48-0.54, y 0.53-0.60, exactly behind the shaft, and wash into pale lavender. Kevin sky (x 0.28, y 0.68) barely shows. The treatment asks for 'cliff glow at its strongest, with every terminal's colour bloom present' and a gold shaft.
fixes.fix: As S01 does, pass a blooms level dict through the shot's build kwargs: for example keys 1.8, strategy 1.6, kevin 1.8, people 1.6, synthia 1.2, operations 1.0, arjun 1.0, linda 1.0. Check that cobalt and yellow separate as two distinct glows either side of the beam rather than mixing. Warm the beam and grade toward gold through apply_look or the shaft colour, so the slot-sun shaft reads gold-white against the paper. Re-check AgX, accepting a slightly olive acid yellow.

fixes.area: Hero envelope seal: passes through the paper and appears on the wrong side (f766-f784)
fixes.problem: I ran a triangle-triangle test on the envelope cache (out/cache/s08/envelope_751_834.pc2). The seal quad cuts through all six fan triangles near the apex on f771-773. Final-quality crops show it there as a dark, half-buried square. From f774 to f789 the seal sits 0.11-0.18 m on the back of the paper while the back faces the lens (the dot product of the front normal with the view direction runs -0.24 to -0.98 from f775 to f784), so the bird shows a cobalt square on its underside from f775 to f781. Before the unfold the seal is flat at z = ENV_PUFF + 0.03, but the 0.5 m bulge falls away under it: its corners float 0.14 m above the paper (0.03 m at the centre) and cast an offset shadow strip, visible on f766 without motion blur. Evidence: crit1-tech/env_seal_sequence.jpg, env_noblock_test.jpg (top-left panel), and the cine critic's crops of f772, f776 and f779.
fixes.fix: In build_envelope, stop interpolating the seal toward z=-0.3 and BIRD[0]. On each frame, place each seal corner on the morphed surface: take the point under the corner on its fan triangle by barycentric lookup and offset it 0.01 m along that triangle's normal. Shrink the seal to zero size by about f773, before u reaches 0.15 and before the back turns toward the lens on f775. Re-run the triangle-triangle check (expect no hits from f768 to f790) and render final crops of f766, f770-781.

fixes.area: Hero bird never reads as joining the flock (lighting and heading continuity, f790-832)
fixes.problem: S08_EnvelopeSun (6 W/m2) and S08_EnvelopeFill (14 W/m2) are linked to the bird for the whole shot. At f832 the bird that should be 'one among thousands' is therefore the brightest object near the arch: display luma 0.85-0.91 against 0.63 for the wall, while every flock bird and near stray reads as a dark core (about 0.42). Measured at final quality in crit1-tech/hero832_final_x4.png. At f832 it is 74 m from the lens and 183 m from the nearest flock bird. Its velocity is nearly perpendicular to the flock's (cosine 0.10), and on screen it moves left (-1.8 px/frame in x) against the ribbon's left-to-right flow (+3.3 px/frame). It ends 56 px from the nearest flock bird, under the ribbon rather than in it.
fixes.fix: Key both envelope lamps down from f790, as the bird leaves the beam, to 0 by about f806. Blend the bird's shading toward OFF_Bird's day look (dark core with a 3600K edge glow) using a keyed mix factor. Steer it with lead pursuit toward a point ahead of the flock's head along the mean flock velocity, so its heading matches the ribbon by about f820 and it ends inside the ribbon's screen footprint at f832.

fixes.area: Foreground wet-stone shelf boils, and the fixed seed does not stop it (f777-832)
fixes.problem: The moving crowds (flock, falls sheets, spray, envelope) catch some of the shelf's shadow, diffuse and glossy rays on every frame, which re-rolls the noise on the glossy wet stone (roughness 0.14). Final-quality crop x 0.12-0.42, y 0-0.2 (the rock area): frame-to-frame p95 |dL*| is 17-19 on f826-829 (animated seed, camera moving under 1.5 px/frame) and still 10.8-13.6 on the fixed-seed frames f830-832. With the camera locked and the swell frozen it is still 9.3. With the crowds hidden it is 0.00, and rendering the same frame twice gives identical images. At 48 spp it is still 8.4, so the GPU sample budget will not cure it. The distant paper wall is bit-identical on f830-832, so the problem is limited to near, glossy surfaces. Raw renders (denoiser off, adaptive sampling off) still differ on 39% of rock pixels, which rules out the denoiser. Evidence: crit1-tech/shelf_static_diff.jpg, shelf_boil_14_vs_48.jpg, shelfprobe/*.png and the shelf_probe*.py logs.
fixes.fix: Tested fix: in the S08 build, set visible_shadow=False and visible_diffuse=False on OFF_Murmuration, OFF_FallsSheets, OFF_FallsSpray and OFF_HeroEnvelope, and set visible_glossy=False on OFF_Murmuration, OFF_FallsSpray and OFF_HeroEnvelope. Keep glossy visibility on the falls sheets so the sea still mirrors the falls. Result for f831 to f832: rock p95 0.46 L* (was 9.3). Side effect: the shelf brightens from 31.5 to 35.2 L* once the crowd occlusion is gone, so re-check its value. Separately, consider bringing the crane to exact rest a few frames before f832 so the fixed-seed frames are truly static. With the crowds on, the 0.3 mm camera shift between f831 and f832 alone moved rock pixels by p95 7.6 L*; I did not re-test that with the fix applied. Tell the env_offline owner: S01, S06, S12 and S14 crowds probably do the same to any near glossy surface.

fixes.area: Accidental glyph: in-focus near fireflies streak (f1199-1203, also f1153-1180)
fixes.problem: OFF_FirefliesNear holds every firefly within 15 m. The ones 11-15 m out (probe ids n2, n4, n5, n12) are sharp at the 16 m focus, but they still have motion blur, because CRISP_FIREFLIES only covers 'fireflies' and 'fireflies_light'. While rising they smear into short vertical strokes with hooked ends, and the denoiser smooths these into solid ticks. At f1201 n5 (13.4 m, about 45 px/frame at 1600) is a green 'l/J'-shaped stroke at the right edge (proof crit1-cine/proof/s12/1201.png, x 776 y 185; zoom in crit1-cine/cmp/tick1201.png). It is about 22 px tall at final. The author's own note already calls a firefly streak a glyph.
fixes.fix: In tune_fireflies() add 'fireflies_near' to the no-motion-blur loop. Then re-probe the lens-side discs n14 (f1167-1190, 2-3 m, about 54 px/frame at 1600) and n16 (f1153-1189) for strobing. If they strobe, ask the env owner to pass build_fireflies(near_bokeh=...) through build_offline and set it to about 5 m. Only the true lens-side discs then stay in the blurred, denoised object, and the 6-15 m points become crisp, unblurred light-group points.

fixes.area: Story beat: Pat's late grey firefly (f1189, f1203) is invisible
fixes.problem: The clock is correct (peaks at f1189 and f1203, locked at f1217), but nobody can see the beat. Pat's firefly is about 248 m away in the arch opening. Because of the 1.4 px rule it is a 2-3 px point, the same size as the other 1,500, and its light grey reads as white. When it peaks the swarm is still at 46% (f1189) and 74% (f1203) of its flash, so it stands out by nothing. In the 1185-vs-1189 crop it is a single light pixel (crit1-cine/cmp/grey_1185_1189.png). Pat's faint grey bloom on the left cliff is also unreadable next to the much brighter shaft haze, so Pat's whole thread in this shot is gone.
fixes.fix: At shot level, add one dedicated Pat firefly: an ico-sphere about 2-3 cm in radius with mat_firefly. Set ff_grey=1, ff_col #8a8a8a, ff_phase=ff_freq=0 and ff_lgain=0, and hide or recolour the swarm's own grey point. Key a slow drift 8-12 m from the lens on the ray to the dark arch opening (screen about x 0.41-0.44, y 0.45-0.55). At f/2.8 focused at 16 m it then reads as a soft, visibly grey disc that is clearly larger than the swarm points. Its lone late bloom at f1189 and f1203 should be the only change in that part of the frame. Check with the probe that it stays in the opening from f1185 to f1217.

fixes.area: Mirror doubling missing at the lock (f1217, f1233)
fixes.problem: The treatment's beat is 'every flash doubled in the terrace water mirrors'. The 3 m rise and the tilt to +10 push the paddy's far edge to about -7.4 degrees, and the frame's bottom edge sits at -9.7 degrees. By ray cast the paddy is the bottom 5% or less at f1217 ((0.5, 0.1) already hits the sea at 113 m) and it is gone at f1233. The far swarm, 2-15 m over the sea and 100-250 m out, can only reflect in the paddy within about 3 degrees of the horizon, so it never doubles there. The rippled sea turns the flash into a dense field of white glitter in the lower-left quarter, pulsing with each beat (r0/final/1217.png, crit1-cine/cmp/final1217_sea.png). It reads as noise or a starfield, not as coloured doubles. The author's note says the doubling is 'kept in frame at every sync point'; that does not hold.
fixes.fix: Keep the black mirror in frame at every sync point. For example, use RISE about 1.2 m and PITCH0/PITCH1 about +2.5/+7. That keeps the paddy at about 15-19% of the frame bottom through f1233, and the crest still arrives with about 8% headroom (y about 0.92) by f1248. Add a report ray at (0.5, 0.12) that must hit OFF_Paddies on f1185, f1201, f1217 and f1233. Ask the env owner for a near layer of about 150-300 fireflies hovering 0.5-4 m over the lens's own paddy and the next one (8-40 m out), so the doubles land in the mirror. Their main body, the terraces, sits behind this lens.

fixes.area: Night grade and contrast: fireflies don't separate (whole shot)
fixes.problem: S12 is flat mid-grey: median 31-36 and 95th percentile 103-124 on f1153, f1217 and f1248. The same world's night in S14 (f1371) has median 12 and 95th percentile 51, and S11/S13 on either side are near-black (median 0-2). The cut in at f1153 is a 5x luminance jump. At the lock the saturated firefly pixels average L 116, which equals the shaft haze behind them (upper right, L 114), so the fireflies separate only by hue. The unison flash moves the frame mean by only about 8%. At feed or phone size (strip in crit1-cine/cmp/cuts.png) the shot reads as grey fog. The brightest region of every frame is the empty upper-right veil of the shaft. The shaft's near surface is about 100 m from the lens and it is 135 m wide, so it is a featureless column, not a beam.
fixes.fix: Bring the world down about 1-1.3 EV for this shot by lowering the night shaft glow and the paper wall's night backlight (apply_values / apply_light_levels). Leave view exposure alone so the firefly cores keep their level. Targets: frame median about 12-15 to match S14's exterior, firefly cores at least 3x the background behind them, and the flash clearly the brightest event on every beat. Recheck the percentiles on f1153, f1217 and f1248.

fixes.area: Arch silhouette and scale: 'all colour lives in the fireflies'
fixes.problem: The treatment asks for the arch silhouetted against the silver shaft. From this lens the shaft stands about 23 degrees right of the arch, so the arch can't be silhouetted against it. It is also lit verdigris-teal (FILLS 0.5) against dark paper. On every flash it takes a pastel blue, violet, pink and green wash from the swarm's light copy (crit1-cine/proof/s12/1217.png and 1233.png). The script already light-linked the island off for this exact 'pastel mottle'. A 110 m monument lit by insects 50-250 m away tells the eye that the fireflies are lamps or the arch is a model. That breaks the scale, which the treatment names as its first risk. The green-lit grass and the riser also put colour outside the fireflies.
fixes.fix: Set FILLS to about 0.25 (the S01 silhouette range) so the arch reads as a near-black shape outlined by the crest's halo of fireflies. Extend the DARK_ISLAND receiver collection on the light copy to the arch's stone and padlock objects. The crest pines can keep a little light, since fireflies actually sit in them. The swarm then lights only the grass tips and water round each flash, as the treatment says.

fixes.area: Framing edges: right-edge terrace riser, box tangent, crest tangent (f1153-f1190)
fixes.problem: By ray cast, the frame's right 7% (x 0.93-0.99) from f1153 to about f1190 is the OFF_Terraces riser 13.8-14.7 m away. It is a green, low-poly lump whose flat-shaded triangles are visible at final (r0/final/1153.png, x 1480-1600, y 600-780). Its edge touches the right end of the meeting-room box (box ends at x about 0.93), so the planted box is clipped by a CG lump. At the cut (f1153) the crest sits exactly on the top edge (y 0.984), right at the legs' junction: a tangent crop on the opening still.
fixes.fix: Offset the lens about 1.2 m to the left, perpendicular to the view azimuth, over the same paddy. Parallax at 14 m moves the riser about 0.08 of the frame width right, out of frame, while the 140-300 m world moves less than 0.01. Verify that rays at (0.97, 0.4) and (0.95, 0.3) on f1153 no longer hit OFF_Terraces. Start the tilt so the top edge cuts decisively through the crest mass (PITCH0 about +2 to +3), not on the junction.

fixes.area: Swarm reads as a flat band of identical dots (f1153-f1201)
fixes.problem: The lens stands about 10-13 m up and looks away from the terraces. The visible swarm is the drift over the sea, 50-250 m out and 2-15 m up, so until about f1201 it is compressed into a band within about 3 degrees of the horizon. The 1.4 px rule makes every point the same 3-4 px with equal brightness at any distance, so there are no depth cues. At final the unison flash reads as a flat overlay of Christmas lights or confetti (crit1-cine/cmp/arch_lower_1217.png), not as a volume of insects.
fixes.fix: Library request to the env owner: past about 120 m, let points shrink below 1.4 px and dim with distance (keep the energy and the 2-3 px floor only mid-field); give each firefly a peak variance of about 0.6-1.0; add the near paddy layer from the doubling fix so the flash spans foreground to far ground. Shot side: the lower pitch from the doubling fix also gives the near layer more frame.

fixes.area: sync / cut out (f1247-1248)
fixes.problem: The last frame of the shot carries a half flash. With FIREFLY_T0=1217 and a 16-frame period, the swarm starts its 2-frame rise into the beat-78 flash at f1249, which is S13's first frame. The flash itself is never seen, but f1248 pops from base glow to about 55%. Measured on the animatic, saturated firefly pixels go 396 (f1247) -> 1907 (f1248), against 2075 at the f1217 lock. So the shot ends on a one-frame off-beat flicker, right as the lens settles and we cut to the black room.
fixes.fix: In s12 build(), after tune_fireflies(), hold the swarm clock at base glow across the cut. For both h['mats']['firefly'] and h['mats']['firefly_light'], add keys to their 'FireflyClock' value node with E.key_value(node, 1246, 1246.0) and E.key_value(node, 1250, 1246.0). At clock 1246, u=13, so the swarm and the grey both sit at base 0.1 on f1247-1248. Re-render f1246-1248 at animatic and check that the saturated-pixel count stays near 400. If a flash on the cut is wanted instead, make that an explicit director decision. As built it reads as an accident.

fixes.area: temporal stability: arch (firefly light)
fixes.problem: Coloured mottle crawls on the arch under the per-frame seed. I rendered final f1217 with seeds 1217 and 7: the crest stone differs by 1.41% mean and 5.1% p95 (8-bit luminance) from the seed alone. That is visible blotchy pink and blue smudging that re-shuffles every frame while the lens moves (f1153-1246). The source is the swarm's light (OFF_FirefliesLight, 1,500 tiny emitters) on the arch. More samples do not help: 42 spp gave 1.38%, and 42 spp with adaptive threshold 0.01 gave 1.31%. Light-linking the swarm light off the arch drops it to 0.44% mean and 2.1% p95, and the arch then reads as the clean dark shape the docstring asks for.
fixes.fix: In tune_fireflies(), extend the existing DARK_ISLAND receiver-exclusion collection on OFF_FirefliesLight with OFF_ArchCore, OFF_ArchFill, OFF_ArchPadlocks, OFF_ArchScree*, and the OFF_PadlockTmpl_* instance templates (all were needed in my test). OFF_ArchPines can stay lit if you want the crest halo; re-measure that case. Verify with two seeds on the crest crop: border 0.32-0.50 x, 0.70-0.95 y. My test scripts are in the scratchpad: cresttest2.py.

fixes.area: temporal stability: sea and paddy band (lower third)
fixes.problem: The lower-left sea band is a field of white specks that outnumbers the coloured firefly doubles. Most of it is env_offline's night moon glitter (sea 'GlintLevel', built as roughly 1 px points for S14's top-down lens). Seen from S12's grazing 1.5 m lens, at f1217 in the mirror crop (x 0.30-0.62, y 0-0.25) there are 651 white specks, and 296 with GlintLevel 0. In the same crop, only about 56-60% of the white specks and 58% of the coloured reflection blobs survive a seed change. The rest is sampling noise in the undenoised firefly light group and in the glossy ripples, and with the per-frame seed it boils every frame. Treatment: 'sea near-black with silver glints', every flash doubled.
fixes.fix: After E.apply_values(h, fr.get('values')), add E.apply_values(h, {'sea': {'GlintLevel': 0.2}}) (or 0). That keeps a few silver glints and lets the coloured doubles read. Re-check with a two-seed crop. The remaining coloured-reflection boil comes from the light group never being denoised. If it still reads as noise in motion, raise this shot's final budget and lower the adaptive threshold in that band, then compare persistence across seeds, or accept it as water glitter.

fixes.area: sync legibility: Pat's grey firefly (f1189, f1203)
fixes.problem: The timing is exact, verified in pixels on final-resolution crops around the grey. It sits at base on f1185 and f1201, peaks f1189 (0.62) and f1203 (0.60), and flashes in unison at f1217 (0.60, rise 0.40 at f1216). But the late flash does not read. On screen the #8a8a8a grey core is a white dot, and an ivory (Synthia #fff1d6) firefly rises through the same opening at about 11 px/frame (f1185 (115,104) to f1190 (114,46) in the 180x140 crop) and passes about 35 px from the grey at its solo peak. It is brighter than the grey (0.69-0.80). A saturated firefly also sits at the bottom of the opening (0.5-0.6). So 'alone in the arch's opening, 4 frames late' is ambiguous at f1185-1190. Note also that the grey only rises into the opening by about f1185 (t_rise 1155.4, z 0.5 m at f1153). report() prints its home position, not its path.
fixes.fix: After the build, take every firefly whose projected path comes within about 60 px (at 1600 px) of the grey's path (about x 705, y 468-495) during f1181-1207, excluding the grey itself. Recolour each one to a saturated hue by rewriting its 42 vertices' 'ff_col' attribute on OFF_Fireflies (index order = the far-object sel), or push it out of the opening. At minimum no near-white (Synthia) point may sit in the opening then. Optionally print the grey's actual path in report() (E.firefly_positions with ids) instead of h['grey_firefly'].

fixes.area: Accidental glyph, tilt-up f1389-1395
fixes.problem: The tilt-up runs along the beam and frames the paper-falls ledge with its thin night trickle hanging from the middle. For 7 frames this reads as a clean white capital 'T'. It is the only distinct shape against flat grey cliff, and at f1390-1392 it is upright and crisp. Evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-linkedin/35346f8e-3086-50e0-b336-b295d0b54106/scratchpad/shots/s14/crit1-cine/crops/whip.png and /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-linkedin/35346f8e-3086-50e0-b336-b295d0b54106/scratchpad/shots/s14/crit1-cine/proof/s14/1392.png. Under the no-text rule this blocks the shot.
fixes.fix: Do not let the ledge and trickle isolate as a T. Best fix: re-route the tilt (see the tilt-read item) so the sweep crosses the sea's waterline on the cliffs instead of the falls. Otherwise keep the falls cropped at a frame edge, or break the ledge's straight bar in this shot, for example by hiding its flat lip from camera over f1386-1396 while keeping the trickle and its mist. If any trace stays, keep it under 2 frames and never upright.

fixes.area: Story: the world tilt does not read
fixes.problem: The finale's punchline ('the whole world is tilting... the sea's horizon rolls and climbs the cliffs... a foam line climbing one cliff') never reads. In the hold the lens looks down at -61 to -64 deg, so there is no horizon or waterline. An A/B with gravity forced level is almost identical at f1363 (only the island's foam ring changes). At f1380 the difference is a half-drowned atoll and a higher arch, which read as fixed geography, not motion. During the tilt-up the sea line shows only at f1386, under a -52 deg camera roll that hides it. No foam line or swell is visible anywhere. A/Bs: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-linkedin/35346f8e-3086-50e0-b336-b295d0b54106/scratchpad/shots/s14/crit1-cine/crops/ab_1363.png, ab_1380.png, ab_1386.png.
fixes.fix: Give the tilt-up a 6-8 frame passage (around f1386-1395, the f1393 flash below it) where the sea's far waterline crosses the cup wall with the lid's level rings or rolled rim in frame as a reference. The sea line should sit visibly 10-12 deg off the rim. Make the crema/foam band at the cliff foot catch silver at night so the climbing line reads. Do most of the -52 deg slot-levelling roll before or after that passage so the camera's roll does not read as the world's. Optionally add a moving cue in the hold, such as the atoll's flank visibly going under over f1363-1380.

fixes.area: Tilt-up frames f1388-1394 are not printable
fixes.problem: About 150 deg of tilt in 22 frames (peaking near 10 deg/frame) plus a 52 deg roll produces 7 near-identical frames of grey cliff and silver veil. They hold no composition and show nothing of the 'vast world' (no horizon, no terraces, no flash). Every frame should be a still worth printing.
fixes.fix: Re-time and re-path together with the tilt-read fix. Slow the sweep where it crosses the waterline and the terraces (the f1393 flash in frame, doubled in the mirrors, as the treatment asks), then accelerate up the beam to the slot. Keep the eased start and end.

fixes.area: Exterior hold look f1361-1383
fixes.problem: The frames are busy and lose the restrained night palette. Fireflies are sized for f1377 (FIREFLY_VIEW), so at f1362-1363 they are 3-4 px blobs, a confetti of saturated colour over half the frame. The sea is covered evenly in white specks (present with gravity level too, so floes or glints, not the tilt) that read as a star field rather than black water. The flooded atoll's palms read as green blobs floating on black water. The arch reads as a blue speckled caterpillar. Only the box, its slot and the beam read cleanly.
